In a World Cup summer, the break felt too inordinate for Carrick, champing at the bit to oversee his first pre-season as United head coach.

United have returned to Carton House for their training base after a productive week there in April.



Carrick has been on the County Kildare hotel’s 18-hole golf course but stresses he hasn’t lined his wallet through any wagers on the fairways.

United are teed up for a promising start to the new season. Excluding summers kiboshed by Covid-19, they have spent their entire pre-season in Europe for the first time since 2002. United’s first two fixtures are against newly-promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town.



Twenty years after he was unveiled as their major summer signing with United in the midst of a title drought, Carrick faces a similar challenge from the dugout.

“I have to say coming in to start with as a player was probably the biggest challenge,” Carrick admits. “I’m not saying this is easier, but it was the biggest challenge.

“It was new. It was a massive step up, coming into a whole different environment of something that I didn’t know.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So that was a huge challenge of adapting to that, and then obviously being here for so long, in different ways, it kind of becomes a bit more of a natural environment and you kind of get used to being around it and it becomes normal in some ways.



“Obviously, I’m in a different position, but because I understand a lot of the other things, it doesn’t make it as big of a jump as I understand the role, and it’s a great role, don’t get me wrong, and it’s a huge, huge role.

“But it doesn’t feel that way necessarily all the time because it feels pretty natural.

“That doesn’t mean it’s easy, but it’s just what I know for so long, and 20 years is a long time to understand the club and what’s worked at times and what maybe hasn’t worked.

“So trying to use those learnings and experiences to help everybody else, really.”

There are parallels with the midfield Carrick nestled into back in 2006 and the midfield he is now coaching.



New signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, as well as Kobbie Mainoo and Mason Mount, are all technical-based players.

Carrick partnered Paul Scholes, reinvented as a deep-lying playmaker, when he joined the club. United won their first title in four years in 2007.

That success seems to be influencing the current overhaul of an area where United are still lacking a specialist defensive midfielder.



“We enjoy seeing different things and your eye naturally takes you to different parts of the game,” Carrick explains. “We can all watch the game and see something a little bit different.

“Just being a midfielder, that’s kind of how I’ve seen the game. In some ways, it helps because you’re kind of connected to all parts of the team over time.

“I’m not saying you have to be a midfielder to be a good coach, but I think it’s just how my reference points are in some ways.

“And what I feel’s worked over the years, what kind of football I think the supporters want to see as well, and hopefully that fits together.

“Naturally, midfield is a big part of the teams that I’ve coached and been part of, because that’s just naturally how I see the game.



“Andrey, for such a young man to come in the way he’s come in, his character, his personality is a dream. Literally, he’s a dream.

“He’s so positive, so mature, so switched on. He wants to learn.

“He comes in straight away and he’s trying to help other players and talk in games and communicate in games, and has that personality where he’s got a real substance to him. Delighted to have him.



“Youri’s a little bit more obvious, probably because we’ve seen an awful lot of him and we all know him.

“But again, the character, the personality, the presence, and the quality on top.

“But being a team player and understanding that and connecting everyone together, I think it’s important we got that right. The two midfielders in particular, I think it’ll give us an awful lot and will give us an awful lot moving forward.”

United want one more midfielder, though. “I think we always want to strengthen in every way, so it depends on, is it going to make us better and is it going to help us, and in what ways is it going to help us? And not for the sake of it. It can’t be for the sake of it.

“But, of course, we want to improve, we need to improve. It’s something that we’re working towards, for sure.”



Carrick was in dialogue with Mainoo during the World Cup after he failed to get a kick for England.

The 21-year-old was the only outfield player Thomas Tuchel did not give minutes to. Carrick had an identical experience under Fabio Capello during England’s miserable World Cup in South Africa in 2010.

“He (Mainoo)’s been great since he’s come back,” Carrick enthuses. “I know from the outside you can look in and everyone goes, ‘You should be happy to be there’. And there’s a part of that, and not taking it for granted, for sure.



“But there’s the other part of as a human being and then as a professional, you want to be playing and so I’ve been there, so I understand it.”

“What did he say to him? Try and appreciate being there as much as you can as well, and try and make the most of it, but then keep doing the right thing and being ready.

“In the end, it worked out as it is, but then he comes back and he’s quite happy to be home with us, and he’s been great this week, come straight back into it.”

Didn’t he find it odd that Tuchel did not play him at all?

“Listen, everyone’s got their opinion. There’s a whole squad of good players, that’s why it’s the World Cup and it’s England, so it’s not for me to say that.



“The biggest thing for me is Kobbie’s in a really good place. I think he feels that, he’s come back and he’s come home and he’s ready for a big season.

“And seeing him this week, it’s been great to have him back and get back on the pitch on Saturday.”

Amazon are filming our sit-down for the start of United’s All or Nothing documentary series, due to air next autumn.



As a United player for 12 years and now seven months in as head coach, Carrick is accustomed to the sight of lenses.

“They’re standing there, so I’ve got to be polite,” he laughs. “They’ve been fantastic and respectful as well, and we’ve got to work through it, of course.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But yeah, it probably seems bigger from the outside than it is day-to-day when we’re working in it as well.”

Carrick will hope they record plenty more good results.

Sports.title: Tottenham urged to raid Man Utd for Marcus Rashford despite Michael Carrick offering England World Cup star olive branch
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM have been urged to launch a shock move for Marcus Rashford.

Former Spurs star Jamie O’Hara is claiming the Manchester United forward could be the “perfect” signing for Roberto De Zerbi.



The former Spurs midfielder believes Rashford could rediscover his best form under the Italian boss, who he says has the man-management skills to get the best out of the England star.

Rashford’s future at Old Trafford remains uncertain after returning to United following a season-long loan spell at Barcelona.

The Catalan giants opted against making his move permanent despite the forward scoring 14 goals and registering 14 assists in 47 appearances as they won LaLiga.

But O’Hara believes Spurs should forget their pursuit of other attacking targets and make a move for Rashford instead.



Speaking on Sky Sports’ Tottenham summer special podcast, he said: “I just don’t know why we don’t go for Marcus Rashford. I really think that Spurs should just go, how much do you want? How much can we get him for?

“I know he’s on £350,000 a week, and obviously Spurs potentially can’t afford that but he’s such a brilliant player.

“If you get him at it with a point to prove, I just think he’s still one of the best players around.”

Tottenham are understood to be prioritising a new left-sided forward before the transfer window closes, with Manchester City’s Savinho and Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo among the players linked with a move to north London.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However, O’Hara insists Rashford would be the statement signing De Zerbi has been hinting at after teasing fans over a potential “bomba” arrival.

O’Hara added: “I think De Zerbi is the perfect man-manager for someone like Rashford.

“He’s a manager who will get the best out of him. I think he’d be a good signing for us.

“The left side is something we still need to address. Mathys Tel is a decent young player, but he isn’t the answer.



“We have got to sign someone who’s a top-drawer player, who gets us to another level and really pushes us on.”

Rashford’s future could become one of the biggest transfer stories of the final weeks of the window, although United boss Michael Carrick has opened the door for him to remain part of his plans.

The 28-year-old is back training with the United squad and could still have a role to play if he can convince Carrick he can return to his best.

Spurs have already spent £237million on six new signings this summer, but their recruitment drive has slowed in recent weeks following the club-record £100m arrival of Sandro Tonali.

With the deadline approaching, De Zerbi is still looking for another attacking addition, and O’Hara believes Rashford could be the man to take Tottenham to the next level.

Sports.title: Arsenal handed chance of stunning Victor Osimhen swap transfer with talks opened
Sports.content:
Arsenal handed chance of stunning Victor Osimhen swap transfer with talks opened

Arsenal are scouring the market for a world-class forward after missing out on Vinicius Junior and with Julian Alvarez too expensive - and Victor Osimhen has emerged as an option

View 2 Images Victor Osimhen could leave Galatasaray this summer (Image: Arife Karakum/Getty Images)

Arsenal have reportedly held talks with Galatasaray over the possibility of signing striker Victor Osimhen. The Turkish club initiated discussions over Arsenal duo Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri, but Osimhen has also been raised, with a stunning swap deal now a consideration.

‌



The Gunners have been on the lookout for a world-class forward in the summer transfer window and previously enquired about Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior. The Brazilian ended up signing a new contract with Real, while fellow target Julian Alvarez is proving difficult to land.

‌



Alvarez is valued at over £100million by Atletico Madrid and is also of interest to Barcelona, forcing Arsenal to look elsewhere. Now an intriguing option has emerged during sporting director Andrea Berta's discussions with Galatasaray over two possible sales.

‌



Martinelli and Nwaneri are among the players Mikel Arteta is willing to offload this summer and Galatasaray are interested in both. According to The Telegraph, the Turkish giants have offered £38.4m for Martinelli and are also exploring a move for Nwaneri, who spent last season on loan with Marseille.

‌



During these talks, it is reported that a move for Osimhen to Arsenal was proposed. The 27-year-old Nigeria international has been one of Europe's most prolific goalscorers in recent years and has consistently been linked with a move to the Premier League, including to Tottenham this summer.

He only joined Galatasaray permanently from Napoli last summer for €75m (£64m) following a successful loan spell. Osimhen has 59 goals and 16 assists in 74 appearances for the club and is under contract until June 2029.

Martinelli appears poised to leave Arsenal after seven years, 62 goals and 278 appearances at the club. He has entered the final year of his contract and has been made available for a transfer alongside Gabriel Jesus, who is of interest to Napoli.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are ready to sell Gabriel Martinelli (Image: PA Wire)

Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are the only players have left the defending Premier League champions for transfer fees this summer. And Arteta knows the importance of sales to help free up funds and space in the squad for new additions.

“There is more that we want to do, because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that,” Arteta said after the 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday. “We’re actively trying to do so – the thing is, in the market, it doesn’t just depend on you, and we’re very clear on that.

‌



“The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we’re going to do it because it doesn’t only depend on us.”

He added: “For the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring more quality to the club,. But again, we’re actively looking to improve that and we’re going to try.”

Sports.title: Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa

Arsenal remain strongly interested in Aston Villa and England central defender Ezri Konsa, who has two years left to run on his existing deal at Villa Park

View 2 Images Arsenal's are not currently prepared to match Aston Villa's £60m valuation for Ezri Konsa

Arsenal have been back in touch with Aston Villa over a potential deal for Ezri Konsa but the UEFA Super Cup finalists' £60million valuation is proving problematic.

‌



The 28-year-old remains the Premier League champions' top defensive target heading into the final stretch of the summer transfer window with head coach Mikel Arteta actively pushing to strengthen his backline.

‌



For now, there remains a notable gap - worth in the region of £20m - between what the Gunners would be willing to pay and the kind of money that would see Villa seriously consider a sale.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have made a verbal approach for Konsa earlier in the window, around the time of their interest in Morgan Rogers, which ultimately amounted to nothing.

But the Gunners never truly threw in the towel as the versatile centre-back, who can also operate as a right-back, ticks multiple boxes Arteta.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He is rapidly approaching his peak and is vastly experienced having just competed in his second major tournament for England. He is also a threat in both boxes and crucially, is homegrown.

Konsa, who is also close friends with Bukayo Saka, hails from Newham in east London and is thought to be open to joining Arsenal, even though he was a boyhood Tottenham Hotspur supporter.

Still, a transfer, at this stage, remains difficult as Unai Emery is counting on the player for the upcoming season.

‌



Villa have also offered Konsa a new contract, his existing deal expires in 2028, and that proposal remains on the table.

Mirror Football understands Arsenal would be prepared to better the wages currently on offer in the Midlands, which may prove attractive for Konsa

Villa are not thought to be under any immediate financial pressure to cash-in following the exits of Rogers (£117m to Chelsea ) and Youri Tielemans (£35m to Manchester United) and there's a desire to strengthen, not weaken, Emery's squad following the 2-1 defeat to PSG in Salzburg.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are in the hunt for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

For now, Arsenal view 16-year-old Marli Salmon is viewed as adequate cover and competition for Cristhian Mosquera at right centre-back but there is still scope to bolster their defensive options without William Saliba sidelined due to a back issue.

An injury to Ben White or Mosquera, would also drastically change the picture with Jurrien Timber still recovering from a minor groin procedure.

‌



Ideally, the Gunners want to sign a profile that can play at both centre-back and right-back, which is why Konsa fits the bill.

Other options, including Tottenham's Cristian Romero (now set to join Atletico Madrid) and Atletico's Marc Pubill have been explored but to no avail. Arsenal will be forced to consider other alternatives if Villa continue to dig their heels into the ground.

Konsa has been handed an extended break by Emery alongside England team-mate Ollie Watkins and goalkeeper Emi Martinez following their involvement in the World Cup. He has insisted that all three players required four weeks of rest, which is why he ruled them out of the Super Cup.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona as Michael Carrick prepares to reintegrate him into the squad

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United picture

Michael Carrick insists Marcus Rashford still has plenty to offer Manchester United this season with it now looking increasingly likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international hasn't played for his boyhood club since December 2024, when he was frozen out by former manager Ruben Amorim. Since then, he has had loan spells with Aston Villa and then spent last season with Barcelona.

‌



It was expected that he would secure a permanent move to the Camp Nou, but their decision to sign Anthony Gordon meant they opted against triggering his £26million clause.

‌



He now returns to United, where he could make his return, ironically, against Amorim's AC Milan this weekend. The Manchester Evening News report both sides believe it is most likely he will remain at his parent club and Carrick is confident he will be a positive presence in his squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction," he said.

‌



"I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting."

Had Amorim stayed in charge, it is inconceivable that the burnt bridges would have been able to be mended, but Carrick has a history with Rashford and has helped to smooth the process.

And while Carrick stopped short of definitively confirming he will stay at United, he described him as 'our player' and said he is being treated the same as anyone else within his squad.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United since December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

‌



Carrick added that he was confident the returning Rashford would bring something new to his options and help balance the squad for the upcoming Premier League campaign.

He added: "We're really calm, we just treat it like anybody else coming into the group and there's obviously this slight twist that he knows the club as well as anybody and that's a real positive.

‌



"He's been here all his career, all his life before the last 18 months or so, to understand what it means. That side of things is natural, that's a given. I know he's got history, but I've got history with a number of the players as well, so that doesn't make that a unique situation at all and treat him as exactly like any other player.

"Bringing him into the group and carrying on as normal brings the good things that we haven't got, and we want to get that balance with every individual player, and Marcus has come back and he's in good form, and it's been good to have him around this week."

Sports.title: Anthony Taylor calls out ex-officials in the media for creating 'culture of fear' for refs
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor calls out ex-officials in the media for creating 'culture of fear' for refs

Anthony Taylor has just called time on his spell as a Premier League referee and he has bemoaned the fear culture, which former officials contribute to

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor has called time on 16 years of Premier League refereeing

Anthony Taylor admits the presence of ex-referees in the media criticising their decisions does lead to "a culture of fear, disrespect and shame."

‌



The former Premier League official has called time on his career, retiring last month after appearing at a second World Cup. He officiated 668 matches in the English game, which included every major domestic cup final as well as 163 international fixtures.

‌



Taylor and Michael Oliver have been among the leading names in the refereeing game for years, but that meant the spotlight on them was increased and their decisions were heavily analysed.

‌



A number of former referees, the likes of Keith Hackett, now have columns with media outlets and are free to cast their opinion on referees and the decisions they make - which Taylor admits had a detrimental impact on the environment officials had to work in.

Quizzed by the BBC on whether that type of commentary bothers him Taylor concedes: "Yes, it does personally, because it doesn't have any balance to it a lot of the time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's just part of the focus that comes with football. When we're dealing with supposedly objective analysis of matches, whether that be an expert ex-player in a studio or an ex-referee, that should be balanced and fair. If it's all one-sided criticism, that creates a culture of fear, disrespect, shame.

"There's a thirst for people to be told: 'Is the decision right or wrong?' And the reality in football is there's a lot of subjectivity and opinion in the middle of right and wrong. But that's not acceptable a lot of the time now."

During his career Taylor had to deal with questions over his conduct with the official making a high-profile error in a game between Burnley and Swansea, which came just days after his stag do in 2017. Taylor would admit it was a "terrible" call, but the timing of his trip was irrelevant.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Taylor admits the commentary from former officials is not helpful

Taylor, who will now take up a role leading referees in Turkey, admits that officials are only human and the outside noise certainly impacts on them.

"Any referee will be lying to you if they said that pressure or that scrutiny did not bother them," he said, "because that's a natural human reaction. One of the challenges that referees face at every level is actually understanding the challenges that we face.

Article continues below

"Fear of making mistakes, external opinion, spectators, managers, parents, media, colleagues. All these things feed into creating self-doubt, lacking confidence, and then things can spiral out of control and you lose the ability to actually have any confidence in what you're doing on the field."

Sports.title: Who is Brian Madjo? The Aston Villa wonderkid tipped to be England's Harry Kane successor
Sports.content:
One game, one goal. That's all it takes for a young striker to put themselves on the list of potential Harry Kane successors, such is the concern among England fans over who'll lead the line once their captain's powers wane.

A despondent Kane admitted in the aftermath of England's heartbreaking defeat to Argentina last month that he doesn't know if he'll play at the next World Cup in 2030. By then, he'll be 36 and likely not the force he was in North America.

That's why England need to start the search for his successor. Step forward: Brian Madjo.

At 17 years and six months old, starting a match of UEFA Super Cup's magnitude is enough to get people talking. But his emphatic first-time finish against European champions Paris Saint-Germain has sparked feverish excitement at Villa Park.

‌



The Aston Villa wonderkid - we can safely label him that now - held off Willian Pacho with relative ease at the back post before firing past Matvey Safonov with his weaker left foot. Although it wouldn't send Villa on their way to victory, it was a goal that announced himself on the European stage.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate READ MORE :

But talent spotters have known about him for years. Born in Enfield, north London, Madjo moved to Luxembourg with his Cameroonian parents at a young age. His dad, Guy, was a striker himself and played for several EFL clubs.

After playing in the academies of Luxembourgish sides Marisca Mersch and Racing Union, French club Metz - then in the top flight - came calling in 2023. He made his debut last season aged 16 and played a further four games for their first team in the first half of the 2025-26 campaign.

‌



Meanwhile, Madjo won three caps for Luxembourg at senior level. But thanks to FIFA's rules on player allegiance, he was able to switch to England, as those caps had come in friendlies.

Madjo has since played nine times for England's under-17s, scoring four goals and providing one assist. At club level, however, his move to Aston Villa wasn't as simple.

Is Brain Madjo the next big thing? Have your say in the comments section.

5 View 5 Images Brian Madjo scored on his Aston Villa debut in the UEFA Super Cup (Image: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images He's already being tipped as a long-term replacement for Harry Kane (Image: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

‌



Signed for £10million in January, Madjo initially couldn't play in competitive fixtures due to FIFA's rules on the international transfers of minors. The 17-year-old's transfer was considered an international one due to his appearances for Luxembourg, whereas Villa argued that he was English - given that he was born there and is a UK citizen.

The Premier League club took the dispute to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and won their legal battle earlier this month. That allowed Madjo to be involved in Wednesday's Super Cup in Salzburg and Unai Emery gave him the nod in the absence of Ollie Watkins.

Afforded extra time off after being part of England's squad at the World Cup, Watkins suddenly faces a fight to be in Emery's first-choice starting line-up. At 30, though, Watkins will still fancy his chances of being Kane's successor himself.

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has enjoyed an impressive pre-season with Aston Villa (Image: Dan Istitene/Getty Images)

‌



Yet his situation at Villa Park could soon be replicated with England. Former Villa striker Stan Collymore reckons that a senior call-up isn't far away. "I guarantee he'll be fast tracked into U21s then seniors by the end of the season," Collymore posted on X during Wednesday's clash.

"England are struggling for strikers, out and out No.9s. We aren't producing them at any senior or youth level. So Madjo (he's raw but his physical dominance of two world class central defenders WILL warrant a look by England scouting analysis) potentially being fast tracked simply addresses a problem.

"Is he good enough? God knows. Is one friendly judgement overkill (he's been very good in pre season and one of Europe's best managers deemed him ready enough to play against the European Champions), no I don't think so. There's a gap in England and looking at him is just common sense."

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has switched his allegiance to England from Luxembourg (Image: Frederic Scheidemann - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



After full-time, Villa right-back Matty Cash was asked about Madjo and described his team-mate as a 'beast'. "All pre-season he's put his body around, scored goals," Cash explained.

"And then tonight he had a few chances as well. He had the header where he probably could've scored and then a good finish. Really happy for him and 17 is still so young. He'll be delighted."

Last year, Luxembourg's technical director, Manuel Cardoni, likened him to Romelu Lukaku - but insists that Madjo can be better. "His profile is similar but, even if we are keeping our feet on the ground, Brian has a more complete profile," Cardoni claimed.

"He is good in tight spaces, really good in terms of positional play. He is also good in terms of going in behind, and he can also feed the ball with both feet. He has huge room for growth."

‌



Plenty of excitement, then. But to offer context for how early we are into Madjo's career, you can't even buy him on Fantasy Premier League yet.

Nevertheless, there'll already be expectation on his shoulders when Villa kick-off their Premier League campaign away to Brighton next Sunday. And with the September-October international break not far away, who knows what Thomas Tuchel is thinking?

Madjo could be rubbing shoulders with Kane sooner than we think - or even breathing down his neck.

‌

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle

Virgil van Dijk was the subject of a transfer tug-of-war involving Liverpool and Manchester City with a phone call from Steven Gerrard proving key

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Virgil van Dijk despite interest from Man City

Steven Gerrard has recalled a phone call he received from Virgil van Dijk when he was being pursued by Liverpool and Manchester City where he delivered a blunt message to the defender.

‌



Van Dijk had established himself as one of the Premier League's best centre-halves and made it known to Southampton that he wanted to move on. A summer move failed to materialise, but the saga was always going to continue come January.

‌



Liverpool would win the race, spending a then club-record £75million to land Van Dijk, who made an instant impact as he helped the Reds make the Champions League final within months of joining.

‌



Gerrard recalls Van Dijk phoning him to so that he could get a greater impression of the Merseyside outfit. The Dutchman wasn't looking for the Liverpool legend to sell him the club, instead seeking a greater insight, but Gerrard did make it clear that Liverpool's traditions far exceeded City's.

The former midfielder recalled during Captains, a new LFC Original: “He phoned me at the time actually. I knew his agent really well. It was City, Liverpool.

“He said to me, ‘I haven’t phoned you to sort of push me one way or the other, because I know which way you’re going to push me. But just tell me a little bit about Liverpool?’

‌



“I just said to him, ‘Look, if it’s about what the clubs stand for and what the clubs are about, you’re wasting your time because I think you already know the answer to that.’ It was an interesting conversation and I was so happy that he chose us.”

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk scored on debut for Liverpool back in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

Van Dijk would enjoy the dream debut, scoring against Everton to knock them out of the FA Cup and concedes he was determined to wear red. “That feeling of, like, I wanted to play for this club so badly, it was so intense," he said. "And the fans embraced me from day one. Scoring also against Everton [on his debut] helped massively too!”

Article continues below

Within 18 months of signing Van Dijk had been named the PFA Player of the Year and proved crucial in Liverpool's Champions League success of 2019. The following year he helped the Reds' end their 30-year wait for a top flight title. Van Dijk remains Liverpool's defensive leader despite turning 35 this summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent

Liverpool are pushing to bring in a winger before the window shuts on September 1 and had earmarked Bradley Barcola's PSG team‑mate Ibrahim Mbaye as a possible option

View 2 Images Liverpool have stepped away from pursuing a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool have cooled their interest in Ibrahim Mbaye after discovering that a combined deal for him and Bradley Barcola could approach €200m (£171m). With the summer window ticking down, Liverpool are intent on signing at least one more winger.

‌



Mbaye, capable of operating on either flank, became PSG's youngest-ever starter at just 16-years-and six months, but his route to regular minutes remains blocked by Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Desire Doue and Barcola. Liverpool's initial interest followed Mo Salah's departure earlier in the summer and continued uncertainty around Cody Gakpo ’s future.

‌



However, Fabrizio Romano reports that Liverpool have now stepped away from a potential move after holding talks with Mbaye's agent. Via his YouTube channel, it is claimed that Liverpool held talks with super agent Jorge Mendes over Mbaye, but PSG quoted the Reds around €200m for the pair.

‌



Liverpool could end up signing two new wingers for Andoni Iraola's squad, especially if Cody Gakpo joins Tottenham, but they believe that PSG's asking price for Mbaye is currently too high. Reports indicate PSG value Mbaye between €40m (£34m) and €50m (£42m).

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool have already added one wide option this summer, bringing in Osasuna's Victor Munoz for £34m, but with Munoz operating on the left, the club still need a natural right‑sided winger to fill the long‑standing role previously held by Salah. Barcola, who was left out of Wednesday's UEFA Super Cup final against Aston Villa, remains an option as uncertainty over his future continues.

‌



PSG president Nasser bin Ghanim Al‑Khelaifi has also declined to rule out a potential departure, telling beIN SPORTS after the match: "We’re working calmly, we don’t talk too much, we do.

"I can’t say whether he will leave or not. Today, he is a PSG player. We’ll see!"

PSG boss Enrique sidestepped a question on Barcola's future, adding: "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

‌



View 2 Images It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will meet PSG's asking price for Bradley Barcola (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Liverpool's chase has hit a major stumbling block, with PSG valuing the 23‑year‑old at around £145m - a fee that would eclipse the £125m Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer. Romano adds that talks between the two clubs are still ongoing, with Barcola himself keen on making the move to Anfield.

With the window entering its final stretch, it remains unclear whether the Reds side will go anywhere near that price. Iraola made his need for a winger clear from the very start of pre‑season. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players," he said.

‌



"Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

So far Iraola has welcomed Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo as well as Munoz.

Sports.title: McIlroy makes woeful start to FedExCup Playoffs as Spieth shares early lead
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy made a woeful start to the FedExCup Playoffs as he shot four-over par opening round at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis.

Playing for the first time since finishing tied for 40th at The Open at Royal Birkdale almost a full month ago, McIlroy was level par going into the final three holes before a disastrous streak left him towards the rear of the field.

Dropped shots at 16 and 17 were followed by a double bogey at TPC Southwind's final hole, which came after McIlroy found the water with his tee shot to the closing par four.

The 74 left McIlroy nine shots adrift of the early leaders, with American duo Jordan Spieth and Michael Thorbjornsen setting the early pace with 65s.

England's Tommy Fleetwood, who was paired with Spieth, was a shot off that mark after opening up with a 66 that included a delightful chip in for eagle at the par-five third hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Fleetwood produced this eagle on third hole at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Fleetwood said: "I feel good. I didn't really play very good in the practice days. Game's not really been that great. I've been showing a lot, like some good and some really not so good.

"Hit it great off the tee today. Still my iron play was iffy, but I did a good job of managing it for the most part. Still hit some really good shots, and you can never underestimate how good - I think shooting under par on this golf course is very good."

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside McIlroy in the marquee group for the opening two rounds, put himself in a solid position by delivering a 68.

Scheffler said: "I felt like I hit a lot of quality shots with my irons.I did a good job of being patient and not trying to force it too much.

"I feel like I was right on the edge of having a good day, kind of all day is how I would describe it. So, I felt like patience-wise, I did a pretty good job."

Fleetwood had European company towards the top of the leaderboard, with Ludvig Aberg and Sepp Straka both joining Scheffler on two-under.

McIlroy could at least take consolation from not having the worst round of the day, which belonged to Scotland's Robert MacIntyre, who shot a 12-over par 82.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Golf Podcast, Jamie Weir and Brad Faxon debate whether Rory McIlroy's extended break since The Open will help him win a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

Memphis is hosting the first of three FedExCup Playoffs events, with only the top 50 in the overall season standings at the end of Sunday's final round progressing to the BMW Championship, and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy's position of 12th out of the 70-player field means there is no concern about his progress to the BMW Championship, while the fact the events have no cut gives him plenty of time to climb the leaderboard over the weekend.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brooks Koepka was extremely disappointed after failing to make the FedExCup playoffs.

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

Live coverage of the first event of the PGA Tour's FedExCup Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship, continues at 5pm on Friday. Watch live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Leicester City up for sale for more than £200m
Sports.content:
Thai owners King Power are seeking to sell Leicester City for more than £200m.

The former Premier League champions engaged with Citibank to sound out potential buyers, it was reported last month.

Sky Sports News has now seen a sales pitch brochure produced by the investment bank, detailing the investment opportunity and the infrastructure which is included for sale at the club.

The dossier lists as up for sale: the men's and women's teams, King Power Stadium, both the women's and the men's training facilities, and OH Leuven, Leicester's sister club in Belgium.

The project is titled "Project Lineup" and values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the sale of King Power's football teams.

In 2023, the club purchased the land around the King Power stadium for redevelopment, with plans to expand the capacity to 40,000, build a new hotel and entertainment complex.

Citigroup forecast the club's revenue during the 2026 financial year to be £97m.

However, the bank do not mention the club's two relegations between 2023 and 2025 and the financial losses that caused.

Image: Leicester City won the Premier League 10 years ago but are now in League One

King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.

In recent years, King Power have converted a lot of debt into equity, to the tune of almost £300m. That has meant, apart from some small maintenance loans, the club is largely debt-free.

Sky Sports News has been told King Power have no urgency to sell, and they will continue to fund the club to the fullest until such time as a new, credible buyer steps forward. They have backed head coach Russell Martin this summer, with nine new signings.

The document states that Leicester is the sixth most successful team in English football since 2000, making this a "rare opportunity" to buy a club with a record of "winning promotions to higher divisions".

Image: Leicester City famously won the Premier League in 2015/16

As well as their surprise Premier League win in 2016, Leicester also won the FA Cup and Community Shield in 2021.

These successes are all included in the sales pitch, but their current position in League One is not referenced.

The document also cites Ben Chilwell, Harvey Barnes and Kieran Dewsbury-Hall as profitable recent transfers, with Gary Lineker and Emile Heskey listed at notable former players.

Sky Sports News contacted Leicester City for comment but they have declined to do so.

Analysis: 'Finding the right purchaser could take years'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"On the face of it, it seems bizarre that King Power would look to sell Leicester City at a time when the club is at its lowest ebb, and at one of its lowest market values, with the team in League One after three relegations in four seasons.

"But in truth Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been seeking new investment for several years - all that is new here is the glossy brochure which advertises the club for sale, accentuating its assets. It is now being actively marketed for sale by financial specialists.

Image: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha holding the FA Cup

"That brochure - unusual as it is - is concrete evidence of a looming end of an era. King Power want out - having delivered unprecedented success in the form of the most unlikely of Premier League titles, an FA Cup, Champions League football and a Community Shield.

"For some Leicester fans, all that success has been tarnished by recent failures, and there have been protests against the ownership, and the director of football, Jon Rudkin. Serious mistakes have been made, for sure, in the management of the club in recent years, which has seen Leicester crash into League One, after boasting to be the club which came closest to breaking the "Big Six" Premier League monopoly over the last decade.

"But those dissenting Leicester fans should be careful what they wish for. On the open market, the football club is a very attractive prospect - almost entirely debt-free (thanks to the generosity of King Power in turning almost all of their £300m debt into equity in recent years) and with fully owned assets that are the envy of much bigger clubs in the Premier League. Their Seagrave training ground is a better facility than all but a handful of others in Europe.

"However, despite all their recent success, Leicester's fan-base is not as sizeable as many of the big clubs in the Championship, and having dropped into the third tier, even promotion at the first attempt would mean they didn't have the benefit of parachute payments in the second tier. All of those facts will be taken into account by would-be buyers.

"So don't expect a quick sale of the club. It could take years to find the right purchaser. The good news for Foxes fans is that King Power will not relinquish their responsibility as custodians, just because they have made the decision to sell. Nine new signings this summer is evidence of their determination to still support the football club. And the goodwill that the Thai business leaders still have for Leicester will almost certainly mean that they won't sell to the highest bidder, just to make a quick buck.

"Khun "Top" knows his legacy is at stake, and in memory of his late father, who died tragically in a helicopter crash in the stadium car park, he will no doubt want to sell the club to a new owner who can take the club forward, and once again make it a success."

Sports.title: Draper beaten in Cincinnati first round after blowing second-set lead
Sports.content:
Jack Draper lost 6-3 7-5 to Martin Landaluce in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after blowing six set-point chances to level the match.

Little more than a week on from a first-round defeat in Montreal on his return from injury, Draper was once more unable to maintain a consistent level as he succumbed to the Spaniard.

After being broken in the first game of the match on his way to losing the first set, Draper looked set to level when he went 5-2 up in the second having secured a double-break.

However, he would fail to take six set points spread across the next three games as Landaluce broke twice to level at 5-5.

Draper saved a match point for Landaluce before bringing up a chance of his own to force a tie break, but he was denied before his opponent closed out the match in just short of two hours.

The 24-year-old appeared extremely glum in the closing stages, but at least appeared to finish the match without any major fitness issues.

During his defeat to Terence Atmane in Montreal, the power of Draper's shots notably dropped off in the third set, while he was also in tears during the changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Draper in tears on return from injury at the Canadian Open.

The circumstances in Montreal suggested Draper had reaggravated the left-arm injury that has plagued him since June 2025, at which point he had reached a career-high world ranking of fourth, but a swift return to the practice courts in Cincinnati calmed concern over his physical state.

While only Draper and his team know his true physical condition, it is clear that he is struggling to find anything like his best form, with the final major of the year - the US Open - starting in New York on August 30.

Sports.title: Doyle: Coppull can strike in the Hungerford
Sports.content:
Our ambassador previews four contests on Newbury's Hungerford Day and assesses the big races at Ripon - both cards live on Sky Sports Racing.

Extra furlong ideal for Hungerford fancy

Coppull showed me enough in the Group One July Cup to convince me he is up to taking the Visit Malta Hungerford Stakes (3.10) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Clive Cox's three-year-old took a long time to get organised at Newmarket where the winner - Comanche Brave - got first run but this strong traveller should enjoy the extra furlong on a more conventional track.

Never So Brave will have his supporters on the back of his second in the Criterion at York over this seven-furlong trip but is struggling to get his head in front this season while Godolphin's Symbol Of Honour is solid but has never won over this distance.

A more interesting runner for me is William Haggas's Extremely Zain, a course and distance winner who ran better than his final placing suggests in the International at Ascot and remains on an upward curve. This is a step up in grade, but he can acquit himself well in an ordinary renewal.

Millionaire sets standard in Geoffrey Freer

Dubai Honour, who has four Group Ones and over £5 million in prize money on his CV, can roll back the years in the opening Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes (1.25) at Newbury.

This eight-year-old has given my husband Tom (Marquand) some of his finest moments in the saddle and, with an excellent record fresh, can make it win number 11 on his return from a summer break.

There is little between Mount Atlas and Tabletalk on their efforts in the Silver Cup at York, but I can't see either finding the improvement needed to lower the colours of Dubai Honour on these terms.

Gamrai went down fighting in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot and, whilst he's in deeper waters now, may just benefit from the change of scenery, having joined George Scott from John and Thady Gosden.

Fire can burn it up in Sprint Handicap

Now he has got his head back in front, Richard Hannon's Wheels Of Fire can put up another bold show in the D&H, Excellence In Nutrition Handicap (1.55) at Newbury.

He beat the re-opposing Hypnotised comfortably at Sandown and a six-pound rise may not be enough to stop him following up under Pat Dobbs, even though that rival is better off at the weights.

Chris Mason's Glamorous Breeze is entitled to go close on her solid performance at Goodwood, but Kinswoman has come up short in Listed and Group company and still has something to prove, even though she's dropping back into a handicap off a reduced rating.

Humam set to build on Newmarket third

Humam's front-running third in a warm race at Newmarket puts him bang there for the TPT Fire Handicap (2.35) at Newbury. I loved the way this former Andrew Balding runner stuck to the task to register his best effort for Stuart Williams since being gelded in the winter.

Racing off an unchanged mark, his most recent form is more compelling than that of market rival Scoville, who has disappointed in both the Royal Hunt Cup and the Golden Mile at Goodwood and needs to improve for this drop in trip.

Eve Johnson Houghton's admirable Great Acclaim has been running well in big races such as the Victoria Cup and Buckingham Palace but needs some respite from the handicapper.

Roxby can initiate big-race double

Malton trainer Nigel Tinkler and his apprentice Alex Jary have a great chance of pulling off a memorable big race double at Ripon on Saturday, starting with Lord Roxby in the William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap (3.25).

Middleham Park's four-year-old returns to the North Yorkshire track in top form after beating fancied rival Dark Cloud Rising over course and distance at the start of the month. He also put a big field to the sword at York earlier this summer and can cope with a five-pound rise against some smart rivals who have a bit more to prove.

Likely favourite Fast Track Harry put in an improved performance in first-time cheekpieces at Ascot last time but I'm not convinced the track will suit while the class horse in the race, Aramram, must overcome a low draw and he ran badly from a similar position in this race two years ago.

Boy can turn on the Magic in Silver Cup

In the consolation race, the William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap (2.55), Nigel runs Magic Boy who ticks plenty of boxes in a wide open, big field dash.

This four-year-old is less exposed than most and showed his potential with a hard-fought win against 18 rivals at York last month before a slow start compromised his chances back there three weeks ago.

Magic Boy is ideally drawn in stall 14 and has previous track form which is always so important at the Garden Racecourse. He has finished second on both his visits but can go one better despite needing a career best.

Another interesting contender is Clive Cox's Mythical Composer who is also potentially well-drawn in stall 15 but needs to bounce back from a poor effort at Goodwood, his first since being gelded.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Celtic sign midfielder Baur on an initial four-year deal
Sports.content:
Celtic have made their fourth summer signing with midfielder Mika Baur joining on an initial four-year deal, with the option for a further year.

The 22-year-old arrives in a deal worth around £6.8m, joining from German club Paderborn, after helping them win promotion from the second tier of German football to the Bundesliga.

He scored four times and provided five assists across 33 league appearances last season, and was named the club's player of the year.

Sky Sports News understand the Scottish champions will pay an initial fee of around £4.5m for Baur, with £2.3m in add-ons making up the deal.

Similar to deals struck with fellow summer signings Camilo Duran, Kasper Høgh and Haissem Hassan, a large proportion of the bonuses will be paid out if Celtic reach the league phase of the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Summer signing Kasper Hogh scored a hat-trick in just his second league game at Celtic

Celtic face LASK Linz in their play-off tie next week, and Baur - who came through the youth ranks at Freiburg before moving to Paderborn in 2024 - could now be registered for that Champions League squad.

On joining the Scottish Champions, Baur said: "It's absolutely the right move.

"It's a great club and I've heard incredible things about the fans.

"I'm in the same agency as Nicolas Kuhn so I called him to ask a couple of questions and he was so positive. He said, if you have the chance, just do it.

"I've had a good pre-season with good matches and tough training sessions, everything. So I'm in good shape and I'm ready to go."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Simeon Gholam explains all you need to know on how the play-offs have changed this season in the Championship

Wolves v Blackburn, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Wolves vs Blackburn

Wolves hold the tag of second favourites for the Championship title at 5/1 with Sky Bet - and rightly so - but I'm always wary of backing teams that have made losing football matches a habit, especially in the early stages of a season when playing a level down.

When assessing the last 10 teams that enter the Championship having taken 25 or points or less in the Premier League, their record across the first five games of the season is poor. Of those 50 games, the relegated team won just 15 - a strike rate of just 30 per cent.

The market has Wolves in at 1/2 here, meaning an implied probability of 66 per cent. That looks a shade too high for me, based on the unknowns still regarding this Wolves side. Also, those 50 games also produced a goals per game average of 2.1 which points towards this being a low-scoring fiddly opener for Wolves, who might be lacking some rhythm.

Tony Mowbray takes charge of Blackburn again and despite his health issues and below-par results at his last three clubs, his teams did only concede 1.1 expected goals per 90 minutes across that 85-game sample size. Under 2.5 goals at Evens with Sky Bet is the bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Under 2.5 goals (Evens with Sky Bet)

Bolton v Preston, Saturday 12.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Bolton vs Preston

Preston had a very strong record away from home against the bottom half last season, losing just three of those 15 games but there was a big over-performance which averaged at 0.9 goals per game when you analyse the expected goals supremacy.

The departure of captain Ben Whiteman to Wrexham and the loss of important attacking contributions from Lewis Dobbin and Daniel Jebbison also give Paul Heckingbottom a problem. He saw his team lose four on the bounce in pre-season and a season of struggle could be on the cards.

Looking at previous seasons, newly-promoted teams in the Championship have a solid record of starting the season full of momentum and Bolton can land favourites backers a winner here at 5/4 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1

Bristol City v Millwall, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

There is a temptation to look at Millwall's third-place finish last season and think: that was a bit of a freak, wasn't it?

I don't think it was.

Millwall were third because they were really good at accumulating points.

They won 24 of their 46 league matches, lost only 11 and conceded just 49 goals. Alex Neil has brought a greater degree of tactical flexibility without taking away the characteristics you associate with Millwall. His teams are organised, competitive and pragmatic but there is more individual quality within this squad than we've seen from many previous Millwall sides.

This summer represents a more substantial attempt to change direction for Bristol City which makes them a difficult team to rate, but with such upheaval this looks a good time for Millwall to go there and do Millwall things. Away win at 17/10 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-2

Middlesbrough v Lincoln, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

If you were judging teams on how well they actually played football rather than simply counting the goals that went in, there is a very strong argument that Middlesbrough were the best team in the Championship once Kim Hellberg took charge.

The underlying numbers were exceptional. Boro allowed fewer shots than anyone in the division and produced the Championship's best shot ratio. They collected 80 points from an expected 83.2 and created 109 big chances while conceding only 68. Few teams have a stronger statistical case for improvement.

Hellberg has had his first full pre-season to refine a side that increasingly carries his identity: aggressive, possession-heavy and designed to overwhelm opponents territorially.

Hayden Hackney has left but Hellberg has the credentials to plug that gap. They look a great bet to win promotion at 5/2 with Sky Bet and can start with a home win.

Sports.content:
British former world title challenger Craig Richards will take on Radivoje Kalajdzic in a 10-round light heavyweight showdown, while Lee Cutler faces Louis Greene in a middleweight clash, on Zuffa Boxing's Johnny Fisher bill at London's Copper Box Arena.

Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.

Richards (20-4-1, 13 KOs) is a world-ranked former British champion who fought Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title in 2021. He won his two most recent fights in 2025, including a knockout win over Dan Azeez last December.

The fight will mark the first time hard-hitting, Serbian-born Kalajdzic (30-3, 22 KOs) has fought outside North America as a professional. The 35-year-old's last fight was a seventh-round knockout victory against Oleksandr Gvozdyk in February.

The Copper Box Arena bill will also feature a 10-round middleweight showdown between British boxers Cutler and Greene.

Cutler beat Stevie McKenna on points when they fought in December 2024, marking the only professional defeat for Ireland's KO king so far.

Image: Lee Cutler and Louis Greene clash at middleweight

Cutler's last fight saw him stop Aaron Sutton in his hometown of Bournemouth in three rounds, while Greene - a former Commonwealth super-welterweight champion - earned a points decision win over Daniel Buciuc in Dublin last week.

Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen is also fighting as part of her professional debut after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

Alex MacMillan, Leon Hughes and Fred Pullen, who is also turning professional, are also on the London bill.

Richards: My story isn't written yet - the time is now

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Having announced he'll face Radivoje Kalajdzic on Zuffa Boxing 11's undercard, Craig Richards believes he'll now be able to be able to get the big fights after linking up with the new promotional company.

Craig "Spider" Richards speaking on Sky Sports News:

"It's a very exciting fight. Everyone knows Kalajdzic can punch, I can punch, we've both been two fighters who haven't shied away from competition.

"We've been in with everyone, we've mixed it, we both probably want to push on now towards that world title and I feel like it's a great opportunity.

"UK vs USA - that mix always goes down well! I'm up for it, I'm excited and I think this is now going to be the best version of me going into the new chapter and I get to go and display what I'm about.

Image: Richards is looking for another shot at a world title

"I feel like my story is not written yet and I feel like I need to write it now.

"The problem we had before is that a lot of opponents were turning [a fight with] me down, saying 'he's a hard fight, he's a long night in the office'.

"Zuffa doesn't allow you to do that, and that means I can get some activity. I can go out there and make a statement."
