Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo unveils shock new look just days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez at intimate wedding ceremony
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has revealed an astonishing new hairstyle in the wake of his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez.

Gone is the black, slicked-back hair and in is a hairdo we never thought we'd see on him: a ginger buzz cut with a high skin fade.

The 41-year-old has been remarkably consistent with his look down the years but, with his fresh trim, it would now be hard to distinguish him from his old Manchester United team-mate Paul Scholes.

This could well be the haircut with which he passes his coveted 1,000 career goals mark.

The Al-Nassr star is on 976 goals for club and country and has a year left on his £488,000-a-day contract in Saudi Arabia.

Ronaldo was pictured returning to training, preparing for the season under new manager Ange Postecoglou alongside the likes of Sadio Mane and Kingsley Coman.

Cristiano Ronaldo debuted a bold new look as he returned to training with Al-Nassr

Just days ago he married Georgina Rodriguez in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, alongside their five children

CR7 finally broke his major trophy duck with Al-Nassr last campaign as they got their hands on the Saudi Pro League.

And on Tuesday he finally achieved his long-time dream of marrying Georgina in an 'intimate and private' ceremony with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Their wedding news came just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids. Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina

Ronaldo, 41, is aiming to score 1,000 career goals and has a year left on his deal at Al-Nassr

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina, in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now who is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Liverpool in dispute over star, 16: Clubs heading for a tribunal after failing to agree compensation deal following player's decision to leave the Reds
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Liverpool in dispute over star, 16: Clubs heading for a tribunal after failing to agree compensation deal following player's decision to leave the Reds

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool and Arsenal are heading to a tribunal after failing to agree compensation for 16-year-old prospect Vincent Joseph.

The highly-rated striker, who had appeared for the club's U18s, decided to leave Liverpool last month despite the fact they offered the teenager a scholarship, which had to be signed by July 1. He declined the offer amid interest from the likes of Manchester United, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

However, it is Premier League champions Arsenal who have won the race for the talented number nine's signature.

They have since been in talks with Liverpool over compensation but they have been unable to find common ground and amid the stand-off are now on a collision course for a tribunal to determine the fee due to the Anfield club.

The last teenager to leave Liverpool for another Premier League side was Isaac Moran.

The 17-year-old England youth international left for Newcastle United earlier this year and signed his professional contract in March. Again the clubs failed to agree on compensation and a subsequent tribunal resulted in a seven-figure fee being ordered payable to Liverpool with the settlement for the midfielder having the potential to reach £5m.

Arsenal and Liverpool are heading to a tribunal after failing to agree compensation for 16-year-old Vincent Joseph

Teenage striker Joseph decided to leave Liverpool last month despite being offered a scholarship

A tribunal ruled in February that Liverpool had to pay Chelsea £2.8m rising through add-ons to £4m after they signed Rio Ngumoha from the Blues

The battle for rising Premier League talents has become all the more costly and cut-throat in recent years.

Liverpool fended off strong interest from Manchester City, Arsenal and potentially Real Madrid to secure 16-year-old winger Josh Abe this summer. They also tied up dynamic attacking midfielder Erik Farkas despite City and United both trying plus clubs from Germany and Spain.

On the flip side, Liverpool previously angered Chelsea when they took Rio Ngumoha away from them last year.

The England international was regarded as the best player in his age group at Chelsea, but moved to Liverpool because he believed there was a better pathway to first-team football.

The 17-year-old left Chelsea in September 2024 and signed his first professional contract with Liverpool a year later.

The Professional Football Compensation Committee (PFCC) tribunal decided in February that Liverpool must pay £2.8m which could rise through add-ons to £4m while Chelsea will also be owed 20 percent of the profit if Ngumoha is sold.

The teenager scored on his Premier League debut in August aged 16 years and 361 days at the time, making him the youngest goalscorer in Liverpool's history.

Sports.title: How Man City will replace Rodri - and the inconvenient truth for World Cup hero that shows they might be better off without him
Sports.content:
Rodri is due in Manchester on Friday, after his planned back surgery following World Cup glory meant he was given two extra days' holiday. But in the context of that rehabilitation and the harsh reality that his future now lies away from Manchester City, it wouldn’t represent a great surprise if the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner did not return to the building for regular pre-season testing.

City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for a central midfielder in the final year of his contract, who was awarded player of the tournament last month. Somebody who often looked physically shot last season, yet was imperious at international level.

There is a balance to strike for director of football Hugo Viana in making sure City maximise Rodri's value while also realising that this orchestrated exit – heavily signposted for a year and solidified by Pep Guardiola's goodbye, with the 30-year-old starting only 18 Premier League games in the last two seasons – likely only ends one way.

Guardiola called it last autumn, that City would not see the best of his metronome all season and that recaptured form would be reserved for the World Cup. The suggestion felt intriguing at the time, more by the way in which it was delivered – a little knowing, somewhat resigned. City’s medical staff were attempting to curb Rodri’s desire to rush various injury comebacks.

There are those who believe his performances Stateside, when temperatures dictated that games were played at a slower pace, prove that there is still nobody better across Europe than him. But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts.

In the Premier League, the win ratio is exactly half with him starting. Without, it is 60.3 per cent. A very similar story plays out from 29 starts in all competitions. Never before in Rodri’s City career have the team won more games in his absence.

Manchester City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for Rodri, who was awarded World Cup player of the tournament last month

But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts

Although not an exact science – City still always concede fewer goals when he’s the deep midfielder – and a small sample size, it does represent a comparison worthy of note.

City, and Enzo Maresca, would prefer to plough on with him, of course. Their movements in the transfer window paint a picture of how this is only heading one way.

Proactive and forceful club denials around interest in Chelsea’s £120million-rated Enzo Fernandez at the beginning of the summer have now given way to silence. Fernandez wants to reunite with his old boss Maresca and those close to him believe the feeling to be mutual. Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million.

City sources say Bouaddi's arrival is not linked to Rodri’s future and that they are pursuing him regardless of what happens, in a window that is threatening to become busy if Tijjani Reijnders and potentially another midfielder leave.

Yet his displays across almost 100 senior games, earning rave reviews for a physicality off the ball and intelligence on it, dictate that he can be ready to impact City’s fortunes. His minutes will have to be carefully monitored and managed.

What seemed apparent on Wednesday, when Elliot Anderson was unveiled to supporters during an event at the Etihad, was that the £116million club-record signing fancies more of a roaming ‘box-to-box’ role than filling Rodri’s void.

‘I’ve spoken to the manager a few times – he explained the sort of things that I need to do,’ said Anderson. ‘There is a lot of running, a lot of energy. It’s to try and control games. That is what I can do.

‘I’ll see where I get used. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that. Kevin De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi (right), the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million

There is a feeling that Enzo Fernandez (left) wants to reunite with Enzo Maresca, but for now Elliot Anderson (right) is the man City have identified as the one to run their midfield

City identified Anderson's aggression and punch in the pass as ideal for the way the Premier League operates these days. Maresca has operated with a two-man midfield in his pre-season fixtures – Mateo Kovacic and Reijnders against Atletico Madrid in South Korea on Sunday – and in that system, Anderson would appear as the one who springs forward, chipping in with the sort of goal he scored away at City during a 2-2 draw in March, arriving late.

Kovacic is ahead of Nico Gonzalez in the pecking order and expected to start Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal in Cardiff. Both Gonzalez and Kovacic have publicly declared that they do not wish to leave this summer.

The physical demands Maresca places upon his midfielders is huge, with Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki vying for the role pushed up alongside Erling Haaland. Maresca is looking at around half a dozen options as part of the two, with that second runner crucial. The way Reijnders crashed the boxes during their friendlies showcased exactly what is being preached on the training pitch.

‘I’ve taken huge confidence knowing that I can perform on a World Cup stage,’ Anderson said, also admitting that he’s still struggling with England's semi-final defeat by Argentina. ‘Obviously I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. I had a big decision to make on who to join and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.’

Sports.title: The rivalry of Britain's glam sprinting golden girls - who ignore each other on the track: Amy Hunt goes for European Championships gold quadruple but Dina Asher-Smith stands in her way
Sports.content:
There has already been a British sprinting one-two at this week's European Championships and another could be on the cards as Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith do battle in tonight's women's 200m showpiece.

Newly crowned 100m queen Hunt, 24, is targeting her second gold of the week in her bid for a remarkable quadruple of golds.

Standing in her way is Asher-Smith, 30, who completed the continental sprint double herself in 2018 and is determined to prove she can still rule Europe.

It is not quite 'master versus apprentice', but this is a fascinating next chapter when it comes to the balance of power in British sprinting - and it comes in the event each of them favour.

Asher-Smith has played down talk of a rivalry in the past, instead saying 'everyone is a rival' on the start line. But there is no doubt she will be determined to get one over her compatriot in one of the most intriguing head-to-heads this week.

Some fans picked up on the pair appearing to avoid each other following the conclusion of the women's 100m race in Birmingham.

Newly crowned 100m queen Amy Hunt, 24, is targeting her second gold of the week

Dina Asher-Smith, 30, is the big rival for Hunt in Thursday night's 200m final in Birmingham

Some fans picked up on the pair appearing to avoid each other after the 100m final

Asher-Smith missed out on a 100m medal but is out for revenge in the 200m final on Thursday

Athletics commentator Richard Newman alluded to the rivalry ahead of the Championships, saying on his Podium Athletics podcast: 'I do think - and I don't want to overhype the rivalry between them - but it's going to have so many more eyes on it.

'I think the media are going to build it up more. I think they're going to be asked about it a lot. I know it's real but the intensity of it could make it even more. The intensity of it is going to rise.'

Both domestic contenders eased to victories in their semi-finals and Hunt is staying zen ahead of the next chapter in her shot at history.

'I would give that a solid eight (out of ten),' she said. 'I knew I needed to put down a really hard turn, kill them to 150 (metres) and no-one was ever going to hang with me.

'I was trying to check the screens as I was in lane eight and figure out who was where to save a bit of energy for the final.

'To be relaxed and happy is the biggest thing. It's trying to stay social and not get yourself too serious as you can kill yourself doing that.

'I'm just trying to stay chill, my coach keeps me laughing and we have fun.'

The Cambridge University graduate's bubbly personality has endeared her to fans and brands alike, with sponsors reportedly queueing up to join forces with the 'relatable' star.

Her Instagram page, followed by 142,000 people, showcases her love of culture and literature as well as her exploits on the track, which have hit new heights since her breakthrough World Championship 200m gold in Tokyo last year.

She was not shy when broadcasting her aim to become the fastest woman in Europe, channelling her love of High School Musical when stating 'I want it all' at the start of the week.

The Newark athlete, who went to the same school in Grantham as Margaret Thatcher, now goes in search of following in Asher-Smith's footsteps with a 100m/200m European double.

Cambridge graduate Hunt's profile has boomed since she won silver in the 200m at last year's World Championships in Tokyo

Asher-Smith has been the queen of British sprinting since becoming world champion in 2019

She was made an MBE for her contribution to athletics in the New Year Honours last year

Asher-Smith was dethroned by her domestic rival over the shorter distance on Monday night but has won more European medals than any other Brit and another this evening would bring her tally to nine.

She finished fifth in the 100m but looked in ominous form in the 200m semis, cruising to victory in 22.49 seconds with plenty to spare.

'When you have so many motivated, talented and hard-working ladies, the important thing is a good lane draw for the final,' she said.

'I don't even know what number (medal) it is as to me every single one is different, every one comes in different circumstances.

'I don't really think about what's gone before or what lies ahead, I'm just trying to stay in the moment and execute.'

Two nights on from Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu's one-two in the men's 100m, this is another domestic duel to savour for a home crowd.

After winning the 100m title at June's Novuna UK Athletics Championships on this track, Hunt said: 'It's so great. It shows that our national championships are one of the best in the world. Dina is one of the fastest athletes on the circuit, so I know I have to bring my A game.'

Novuna is the Official Finance Partner of British Athletics and proud sponsor of the GB & NI Athletics Team. Find out more at www.novuna.co.uk.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim wields the axe at AC Milan: Former Man United boss tells SEVEN stars they have no future at the club - including Chelsea flop - as he implements his five-at-the-back system
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim wields the axe at AC Milan: Former Man United boss tells SEVEN stars they have no future at the club - including Chelsea flop - as he implements his five-at-the-back system

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan stars that they have no future with the Italian giants as he implements a brutal cull in his first summer at the club.

Former Chelsea stars Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku are among the group being driven out by the former Manchester United boss.

Amorim took charge at the San Siro in early June, just over six months after he was sacked by the Red Devils, where he won only 38.1 per cent of his games.

He has got off to a poor start in charge of the Rossoneri, drawing against Celtic and arch rivals Inter as well as losing 3-0 against Chelsea last Saturday.

But the Portuguese coach will have the chance to put things right against his old employers in two days' time as Milan face United in Wroclaw, Poland.

Alongside Tomori and Nkunku, he has put Youssouf Fofana, David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano up for sale.

Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan players they no longer have a future at the club

Former Chelsea flop Christopher Nkunku will be shown the door, Daily Mail Sport understands

Tomori has had interest from Coventry City, managed by his old boss Frank Lampard, while Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest, and Villarreal are looking into Fofana.

Amorim held a crunch meeting with club bosses today to discuss his plans for the season, which inevitably involve instituting his five-at-the-back system which failed at Old Trafford.

He has accepted the task of transforming Milan's fortunes after they finished fifth last season in Serie A, missing out on the Champions League.

Another of his tasks will be to sort out the future of Rafael Leao, who has been linked with Galatasaray and Leeds. The winger has been actively looking for a club.

Amorim is ready for the challenge, and suggested that his task at the San Siro is even bigger than at Old Trafford.

'I'm really very happy to be here, it's an honour to be the coach of Milan,' he said.

'Why did I choose Milan? If you read an old interview of mine you will understand it, for me a special club.

'It's a very big challenge that I accepted even if after the last one [at Manchester United] I told myself to accept a smaller one.

'Perhaps it is a greater challenge than the last. I'm proud to be here, we all are, me and my staff.

Fikayo Tomori is another of the seven stars who Amorim hopes will be saying arrivederci

'I'm at Milan to win, if you're Milan coach you have to have this mentality.

'I'm not naive, I know there's a lot of work to do, but if you're the Milan coach you have to play to win.'

Milan last won the Serie A title in the 2021-22 season under Stefano Pioli.

Last campaign they were managed by Massimiliano Allegri, who had been previously had successful spells at the Rossoneri as well as Juventus but struggled to replicate this despite them having no European football.

Sports.title: 'We can achieve something really special': Man United boss Michael Carrick on aims for new season, the future of Marcus Rashford and why Andrey Santos is a 'dream'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick strides in to a plush conference room here at Carton House, the five-star spa hotel which has been home to Manchester United all week, with a big smile on his face. There's a lot for the United boss to be happy about, after all.

Back home his daughter, Louise, has collected her A-Level results and, here in Ireland, the late returns of Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Lisandro Martinez from the World Cup have added a fresh dynamism to a group who overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park only a few hours earlier.

Carrick, unlike predecessor Ruben Amorim, is level-headed. When the tough questions come his way, bosses are relaxed that Carrick won’t rock the boat like Amorim, who United face on Saturday in Poland when they play AC Milan, would do.

It’s why United were comfortable throwing open the doors to Amazon filmmakers for this season’s ‘All or Nothing’ behind-the-scenes documentary.

But don't mistake his calmness for ambivalence. Carrick is determined to win, too.

This has been a summer where top four rivals Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham have all spent north of £100million. Even newly-promoted Coventry and Ipswich have spent more than Manchester United. His message here, though, was crystal clear to those upstairs.

Man United boss Michael Carrick spoke to reporters on the club's pre-season trip to Ireland

United overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park in a friendly on Wednesday evening

'It can't be for the sake of it, but yeah, of course, we want to improve, we need to improve,’ Carrick says. ‘It's something that we're working towards, for sure.’

So far only Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow have arrived to strengthen the first-team squad. Tynan Thompson, an £8m pick-up from Tottenham, is seen as one for the future.

‘I have to say, Karl, Andrey, and Youri, are exactly what we hoped, exactly what we expected in every way,’ he adds.

‘Andrey, for such a young man to come in the way he's come in, his character, his personality is a dream. Literally, he’s a dream.’

But Carrick knows he needs more. United still need a left back - there have been two failed approaches for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall this summer - and another central midfielder remains on the agenda.

By the time this conversation draws to a close, Carrick had referenced a need to ‘push’ in the transfer market four times.

'I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but of course we would like more,’ he continued. ‘We would like more, we need to keep pushing for more.

‘There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious.’

Director of football Jason Wilcox is here in Ireland and remains in ‘constant communication’ with Carrick.

With a frugal approach to the summer so far, one which has so far seen them fail to land top target Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers, and others, can Manchester United seriously contend for a Premier League title this season?

‘I think you've got to have the belief, you've got to be going into the season thinking we can achieve something special,’ he says, reluctant to commit to any bold proclamation for the season ahead.

‘Don't be going into a season thinking this could be a struggle. We've got to set out to really achieve something.

‘We've definitely got the potential to achieve something really special. I'm not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that.

‘I'm not going to make any crazy predictions, but I think on the back of what we've done, I keep saying it, I think that gives us the confidence to move forward. How quickly we keep moving forward, that's the challenge.’

Carrick has been impressed with United's three summer signings so far, particularly Andrey Santos, but he wants more players to come through the door

Carrick was also full of praise for Marcus Rashford, who returned to the club on Sunday

There remains a question mark over Marcus Rashford and the prospect of his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt since 2024, when Amorim left him out in the cold, this weekend.

United have long been open to moving the £325,000-a-week attacker on as part of a plan to reduce the wage bill. They have also been in the market for a left winger all summer, with Crysencio Summerville among the targets, before he opted to move to Saudi Arabia.

Barcelona passed up on their buy option to sign Rashford, who is now back and training well.

‘He's a very good player, Marcus, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in maybe a different direction,’ Carrick adds, before electing not to go as far as ruling out a potential move before the deadline.

‘I think there's ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much.

‘He has done (in the past), and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting.’

There’s a return for Kobbie Mainoo too. Carrick kept in touch with Mainoo all summer via text, checking in as he went through the entire World Cup without playing a minute.

There’s no concerns though. In fact, Carrick believes the Mainoo that has come back is ready to take the Premier League by storm.

'The biggest thing for me, Kobbie's in a really good place,’ he adds. ‘I think he feels that. He’s come back and he's come home and he's ready for a big season.’

But there are lingering concerns over squad depth with United competing back in Europe this season.

‘We're not naive, we know what we're going into,’ he concludes, pressed on the fact that United are facing the prospect of 15-20 more games than last season’s historically low total of 40.

‘But we feel we're a stronger group now than we were last season as well in many ways, so we've just got to capitalise on that.’

Sports.title: Travis Kelce 'is DONE', NFL insider claims as he warns Taylor Swift's husband is set for another bleak Chiefs season
Sports.content:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is 'done' as an elite force in the league after his whirlwind summer, according to one NFL insider.

Kelce has had a life-changing offseason, tying the knot with pop megastar Taylor Swift in a lavish and star-studded private ceremony at Madison Square Garden on July 3 before details of their secret honeymoon were revealed.

But it is now all down to business for the 36-year-old as he enters his 14th and potentially final NFL season. The Chiefs' training camp is in full swing ahead of their first preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday.

However, ahead of their clash, NFL insider Jason La Canfora claims that scouts in the league have suggested the tight end is finished at the top level.

'Kelce is done. That's over. What you saw last year, that's what he is,' Canfora claimed that one NFL scout told him, according to Casino Guru News.

The brutal assessment comes shortly after social media users claimed that Kelce had returned to Chiefs practice with a 'dad bod' after his whirlwind summer.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is 'done' as an elite force in the NFL after his whirlwind summer

Kelce and Swift tied the knot in a star-studded ceremony in the center of Manhattan last month

Swift and Kelce were married in a lavish Madison Square Garden ceremony on July 3

The 36-year-old endured one of his toughest seasons of his NFL career last year, as the Kansas City Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014.

On Wednesday afternoon, Kelce openly admitted that he felt partly to blame for the team's struggles and will look to rectify that during his 14th NFL season.

When asked about what he wants to improve, Kelce said: 'Just being a better leader.

'When we get stuck, with adversity hitting, who's going to want you in that foxhole with you? That's one of those things, I want to be one of those guys that everybody counts on to be there and get us out of that foxhole.'

'There were things I could have done better in that regard,' Kelce added.

Asked about how practice was going, he said: 'I feel ready to rock and roll. Just trying to make sure I set that example for the guys around me, that this is the standard.'

Elsewhere on Tuesday afternoon, Kelce finally shed some light on his star-studded and highly secretive wedding with popstar Swift.

While his focus is back on football for the time being, the tight end could not avoid inevitable questions about his offseason activities in his first press conference this season, saying his 'crazy' wedding was the 'best night of his life'.

Kelce said: 'It was a fun offseason, man, wedding was the best night of my life and I appreciate everyone who came out and celebrated and had fun with us.

Kelce openly admitted that he felt partly to blame for the team's struggles last season

Some fans joked that Kelce had returned to Chiefs practice with a 'dad bod' after his summer

'That's about all I really got from that night. It was a crazy night. It was full of a lot of celebration. But it's football, baby.'

Asked specifically about getting married at Madison Square Garden, he added: 'MSG, man. You know, I always told myself I'd go for a playoff game when the Knicks were rocking. Then my wife went when I was stuck in minicamp, so I didn't get my opportunity to go then.

'So it's kind of cool to be able to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the Mecca of all sports venues, being able to get married in there.

'I can't thank the owners of MSG for allowing us to get the opportunity to do that, knowing we wanted a private event and everything, so it was perfect. And the AC was perfect, man, that's the best part.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
