World.title: Haske advocates investment in youth to secure Nigeria’s future
World.content:
Businessman, politician and development advocate, Abdulrahman Haske, has reaffirmed his belief in the capacity of young people to drive economic growth, social progress and political transformation in Adamawa State, the Northeast and Nigeria, provided they are given access to opportunities, skills and leadership platforms.

Mr Haske made the assertion while speaking as a guest lecturer at the Dinner Lecture organised to commemorate International Youth Day 2026 by the Office of the Adviser to the Adamawa State Governor on Youth Empowerment, in collaboration with the Adamawa State Government, at the Banquet Hall, Government House, Yola.

Speaking on the sub-theme, “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” Haske noted that despite their differing realities, young people across Nigeria share common aspirations: quality education, decent jobs, security, dignity, entrepreneurship opportunities and meaningful participation in governance.

According to him, Nigeria’s youthful population remains one of its greatest assets, but unlocking its potential requires deliberate investment, particularly in regions facing developmental and security challenges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Highlighting conditions in the Northeast, Mr Haske said conflict, poverty, displacement and limited economic opportunities continue to undermine youth development. He referenced data from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) showing that about 2.8 million children across Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States require education-in-emergencies support, while hundreds of schools remain closed and many classrooms have been damaged or destroyed by conflict and insecurity.

Describing the figures as a wake-up call, Mr Haske said the educational crisis extends beyond the classroom and directly affects employability, entrepreneurship, innovation and long-term economic growth.

“For Adamawa, these are not just statistics. These are our communities, our children and our future workforce. While significant efforts have been made, we must be honest that more needs to be done to ensure that every young person can learn, grow and contribute meaningfully to society,” he said.

He stressed that youth empowerment must move beyond rhetoric to practical interventions that provide young people with quality education, digital and technical skills, mentorship, access to capital, technology and markets.

“Young people need more than slogans about empowerment. We must create conditions where businesses can grow, innovation can thrive and jobs can be created at scale,” Haske noted.

The entrepreneur further called for a comprehensive youth agenda for the Northeast that links education to skills acquisition, skills to employment, entrepreneurship to markets and political participation to real decision-making. He also advocated rebuilding damaged learning infrastructure and ensuring uninterrupted access to education as critical components of sustainable development.

On governance, Mr Haske urged greater inclusion of young people in leadership and decision-making processes. “Young people should not simply be mobilised during election cycles. They must be empowered to participate, contribute ideas and take leadership responsibilities. Politics must become a platform for service, innovation and problem-solving,” he said.

He noted that while young Nigerians face different challenges, their aspirations remain the same.

“A young entrepreneur in Abuja may worry about finance and market access, while a young person in Adamawa may be dealing with displacement, insecurity or interrupted education. Yet both desire a fair opportunity to build a meaningful life,” he added.

Mr Haske urged government, the private sector, development partners and community leaders to increase investments in education, agriculture, entrepreneurship, digital literacy, technical training and the creative economy, noting that such investments would reduce poverty and unemployment while empowering young people to become drivers of development.

Addressing young people directly, he encouraged them not to allow present circumstances to define their future.

“Keep learning. Keep building. Stay involved in your communities and prepare yourselves to lead. The future of Adamawa and Nigeria will be shaped by young people who are willing to innovate, create solutions and serve,” Haske charged the youths.

Reaffirming that young people are an asset to be invested in, Haske called on leaders to move beyond symbolic celebrations and focus on building systems that create opportunities every day.

“We cannot afford to lose another generation to poverty, insecurity or lack of opportunity. The reality that 2.8 million children across Adamawa, Borno and Yobe still require emergency education support should challenge all of us to act with urgency. Investing in our young people today is the surest path to achieving inclusive growth, lasting peace and sustainable development,” he said.

Signed:

Abdulgaffar Ahmed

Publicity Secretary to Hon. Abdulrahman Haske

Yola, Adamawa State

13 August, 2026

World.title: OsunDecides: Accord dismisses Imumolen’s endorsement of APC candidate, reaffirms Adeleke
World.content:
The leadership of Accord Party in Osun State has distanced itself from Christopher Imumolen’s endorsement of the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, insisting that Governor Ademola Adeleke remains Accord Party’s candidate for Saturday’s election.

The development came hours after Mr Imumolen appeared at the APC’s final campaign rally in Osogbo on Thursday, where he declared that Accord had withdrawn its support for Mr Adeleke and directed the party’s members to vote for Mr Oyebamiji.

But in a statement issued in Osogbo on Thursday, the Osun State chapter of Accord rejected the endorsement, describing Mr Imumolen as an “impersonator” and insisting that he does not represent the party’s leadership.

The statement, signed by the state chairman, Victor Akande, said the party’s recognised National Chairman remains Maxwell Mgbudem and that the party’s National Working Committee had not endorsed any candidate other than Mr Adeleke.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The Accord Party and its National Working Committee still recognises Senator Ademola Adeleke as its only candidate for the Osun Governorship election,” the statement said.

The party urged voters to disregard Mr Imumolen’s declaration, which it described as an attempt to create confusion within the party days before the election.

At the APC mega rally earlier on Thursday, Mr Imumolen introduced himself as the National Chairman of Accord and announced that the party had withdrawn its support for Mr Adeleke.

“As the national chairman of [the] Accord Party, we have taken down our support for Ademola Adeleke and today, we declare our support for Ambo (Oyebamiji),” he said.

What is behind the competing claims?

The dispute is rooted in a longstanding leadership crisis within Accord, with both Mr Imumolen and Mr Mgbudem having at different times laid claim to the leadership of the party.

However, INEC’s latest records list Maxwell Mgbudem as the National Chairman of Accord and Adebukola Abiola as National Secretary.

The Mgbudem-led leadership has previously rejected Mr Imumolen’s claim to the chairmanship. In April, Mr Mgbudem said Mr Imumolen had been expelled from the party and described his attempt to claim the chairmanship as illegitimate.

Mr Imumolen, however, has continued to claim that he is the authentic national chairman and in April led supporters to INEC’s headquarters in Abuja demanding recognition. Reports at the time documented the competing claims, while noting that INEC recognised the Mgbudem-led leadership.

The disagreement has also spilled into the party’s activities ahead of elections, with competing factions conducting separate political activities and claiming authority over the party structure.

Against this background, Mr Imumolen’s appearance at the APC rally and endorsement of Mr Oyebamiji has now triggered another confrontation between the two camps.

Accord: ‘Adeleke remains our candidate’

Mr Akande, the Osun Accord chairman, said the party was “highly embarrassed” by what he described as the endorsement and accused the APC of attempting to exploit the party’s internal dispute.

He alleged that the APC had previously attempted to create divisions within Accord by supporting a parallel leadership structure.

“The public should take note that the Accord Party and its National Working Committee still recognises Senator Ademola Adeleke as its only candidate for the Osun Governorship election,” he said.

He also described the APC’s action as “desperation” ahead of Saturday’s election and urged Osun voters not to be misled by the endorsement.

World.title: Lalong mourns former Plateau Assembly Speaker, Peter Azi
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

Senator representing Plateau South Senatorial District, Simon Lalong, has mourned the death of former Speaker of the Plateau State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Peter Azi.

Lalong, who is also a former governor of Plateau State, described Azi’s death on Thursday as a painful and devastating loss to his family, constituents, Plateau State and the political community.

In a condolence message, Lalong recalled the contributions of the deceased to the development of Plateau State, particularly his service as Speaker during the administration of former Governor Jonah Jang.

He described Azi as a trusted political ally and committed member of the All Progressives Congress, APC, who remained dedicated to serving the people, particularly at the grassroots.

According to Lalong, Azi distinguished himself through his commitment to public service, humility and loyalty, adding that his contributions to the political development of the state and the strengthening of democratic institutions would not be forgotten.

Lalong also described Azi as a committed member of the Conference of Former Speakers of State Houses of Assembly of Nigeria, COFFSHA, which he leads.

He said the deceased actively identified with the objectives of the association and remained passionate about promoting good governance and strengthening the legislature.

Lalong said: “Peter Azi was not only a former Speaker and distinguished public servant; he was a brother, a dependable political ally and a strong member of our political family.

“His death has left a painful void that will be difficult to fill. His commitment to the people and his contributions to Plateau State, particularly at the grassroots, will continue to be remembered.”

The former governor, on behalf of his family, the people of Plateau South Senatorial District and COFFSHA, extended his condolences to the Azi family, friends, political associates and the people of Plateau State.

He prayed God to grant the family the strength and fortitude to bear the loss and grant the soul of the former Speaker eternal rest.

Lalong urged the family to take solace in the worthy legacy left by Azi and the lives he touched during his years of service to humanity.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul.

World.title: ‘Osun Govt gave me car, not you’ — Oyinlola denies Adeleke’s claim
World.content:
Former Osun State Governor Olagunsoye Oyinlola has denied Governor Ademola Adeleke’s claim that he requested and received a new vehicle before endorsing the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, ahead of the August 15 election.

Oyinlola described Adeleke’s allegation as untrue, saying the vehicle he received was provided by the Osun State Government in accordance with a law governing the benefits of former governors.

He spoke in an interview with Channels Television while responding to Adeleke’s claim that he gave him a car.

“That is far from the truth and it is a bad development that a governor will continue to tell lies,” Oyinlola said.

According to the former governor, the Osun State House of Assembly enacted legislation prescribing certain benefits for former governors, including the replacement of their official vehicles every four years.

He said the vehicle was therefore not a personal gift from Adeleke, but an entitlement provided under state law.

“It wasn’t Ademola that gave me vehicle. It was the Osun State Government, it is a law of the state enacted by the House of Assembly,” he said.

Oyinlola, who left office 16 years ago, argued that he was entitled to vehicles that should have been replaced during the period since he left office.

“I’ve been out of Osun State government since the last 16 years. If you aggregate it, it means the state is still having to give up three vehicles,” he said.

He also explained that the legislation provides other benefits for former governors, including security and domestic staff.

“There are other things, like my security should be taken care of. The police should be paid for, the cook should be taken care of and the drivers. Those are the requisite of that enactment,” Oyinlola said.

The former governor’s response comes amid heightened political activity in Osun ahead of Saturday’s governorship election, in which Adeleke is seeking re-election while Oyebamiji is the APC candidate.

World.title: I have no regrets backing Oyebamiji – Oyinlola
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Former Osun State Governor, Olagunsoye Oyinlola, has said he has no regrets supporting the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Biodun Oyebamiji, ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

Oyinlola gave two reasons for withdrawing his support for Governor Ademola Adeleke, accusing the governor of joining the Accord Party without adequate consultation and concentrating major projects in his own area.

He also dismissed Adeleke’s claim that he bought him a car, saying the vehicle was provided by the Osun State Government in line with an existing law.

He spoke on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, on Thursday.

On his reasons for declaring support for Oyebamiji, he said: “First, when the political party (Peoples Democratic Party) was hit by serious turbulence at the national level, we foresaw that it would eventually affect us at the state level. So, we thought of a way out. And that was why we were thinking of an alternate platform for our candidate to run with. Though we started the discussion with … and the governor with the agreement that when they return from Atlanta, we will have a stakeholders’ meeting. Surprisingly, that did not come up. We only just saw on the social media that Mr Governor had resigned from our party and he had ported to the Accord Party.

“If you have to go back in history, the policy thrust of the founding fathers of Osun State was that there should be even and equal development of the state all around. What we have witnessed under the regime of Governor Adeleke is different. As of today, government has executed about 20 major projects around the senatorial districts. Out of the N362 billion spent altogether, N260.5 billion was spent in Ede. When you skew things in preference to your own area it does not augur well.”

On the governor’s claims of purchasing him a car, he said: “That is far from the truth. It is a sad development that the governor will continue to tell lies. The Osun State House of Assembly enacted a law whereby some … will accrue to whosoever has governed the state. One of the things that should accrue to a former governor is that for every four years, his vehicle should be changed.

“I have been out of Osun State government in the last three years. It wasn’t Ademola that gave me the vehicle. It was the Osun State government. It is a law of the state enacted by the House of Assembly. For him to misinform is a sad development for the chief executive of the state. There are other things like my security that should be taken care of. The police attached to me should be paid for, the cook should be taken care of and the drivers.

“By the grace of God, I started buying a car when I was 21. When I was going to Government House, I went with my entire convoy. Why will he paint it like I went to beg? It is a very sad development. He should say it the way it is, and that it is a law, it is my entitlement and he still owes me three more vehicles.”

On other reasons for withdrawing support from Adeley, he said: “As the party, the engine oil that services a political party is a constant meeting. Today, anything pertaining to the party, you have to head to Ede. Our party headquarters in Osogbo has never for a long while held any meeting. And that is the arena through which politicians will rub their minds.”

On whether his decision contradicted his philosophy, he said: “Let us get the facts right: it was because of what PDP did to me that made me support former Governor Rauf Aregbesola four days to the then election. That was the fact that changed the time of things. The PDP never kept to the agreement. As an officer who served for 30 solid years in the Nigerian army, we do not jump into conclusions. You do appreciation and you draw up your conclusion that will lead you to a positive end. I think I have done that. I have no regrets whatsoever.”

World.title: 1.9 million PVCs collected in Osun ahead of Saturday’s election
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Omeiza Ajayi

The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC on Thursday said a total of 1,906,390 Permanent Voter Cards PVCs, representing 81.50 per cent of registered voters, have been collected across Osun State ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement announcing the final figures of PVC collection in the state.

According to the statement, out of the 2,339,233 registered voters in Osun State, the remaining 426,842 PVCs, representing 18.50 per cent, have not been collected and have been safely deposited with the Central Bank of Nigeria CBN, in line with the Commission’s established practice.

The statement also disclosed that some voters whose PVCs were damaged, defaced, or lost applied for replacement cards, with 6,101 of those applicants successfully printing downloadable copies of their PVCs.

INEC added that a table showing the PVCs collected on a Polling Unit by Polling Unit basis has been published on its website for public access.

The commission reassured political parties, civil society organisations, the media, and residents of Osun State of its preparedness to deliver a credible poll on Saturday, 15th August 2026.

“The Commission reassures political parties, civil society organisations, media, and the good people of Osun State of its total readiness to conduct a free, fair, credible, transparent, and inclusive election on Saturday, 15th August 2026,” the statement read.

World.title: FG moves to end aviation row as airlines, unions agree on fresh measures
World.content:
Keyamo

By Nnasom David

The Federal Government, aviation sector unions and airline operators have reached a number of resolutions aimed at resolving lingering issues in the industry.

Vanguard reports that this followed an emergency meeting convened by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, after tensions rocked operations at Abuja and Lagos airports.

The meeting, held as a follow-up to previous engagements with aviation unions and the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON) after the temporary suspension of the unions’ industrial action on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, was aimed at promoting cooperation and stability in the aviation sector.

A statement signed by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mahmud Adam Kambari, said the parties agreed on measures to address outstanding financial obligations between airlines and aviation agencies.

According to the resolutions, the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and heads of other aviation agencies will obtain payment schedules from airlines, taking into account airlines’ operational costs and prevailing economic realities.

The statement added that directors of finance and accounts across aviation agencies are expected to meet individual airlines within one week to agree on realistic repayment plans.

The meeting also addressed the issue of workers’ rights to belong or not belong to unions.

Keyamo affirmed that workers have the right to independently decide whether they want to join unions without interference from airline management.

The NCAA was consequently directed to ensure that unions have direct access to employees of all airlines for the distribution of union membership forms, allowing workers to make their decisions freely.

Furthermore, Keyamo warned that any airline that prevents unions from having direct interaction with workers would face sanctions from the NCAA.

The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review progress made and assess the state of the issues discussed.

The minister, more so, assured stakeholders of the government’s commitment to maintaining a safe, efficient and sustainable aviation sector.

Keyamo further reiterated President Bola Tinubu’s commitment towards ensuring peace, safety and growth in Nigeria’s aviation industry.

World.title: Ghana’s Black Queens qualify for World Cup playoffs
World.content:
Ghana’s Black Queens staged a second-half comeback to defeat fellow West Africans Côte d’Ivoire 2-1 and book their place in the Intercontinental World Cup Playoffs scheduled for December.

Ghana dominated possession for large periods of the encounter but found themselves behind before half-time after Côte d’Ivoire converted a penalty to take a 1-0 lead into the break.

The Black Queens responded strongly after the restart, eventually drawing level with a headed effort to put the game back on level terms.

With the match heading towards its conclusion, Germany-based Josephine Bonsu stepped up from the penalty spot and calmly converted a late spot-kick to complete Ghana’s comeback and secure a 2-1 victory.

The result means Ghana will now advance to Phase 1 of the Intercontinental Playoffs in December, where they will be joined by either Nigeria or South Africa.

The playoffs will determine qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil, with Ghana now one step closer to securing a place at the global tournament.

Vanguard News

World.title: FG denies postponing paramilitary recruitment, says exercise ongoing
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The Federal Government has denied claims that the ongoing recruitment exercise by the Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board, CDCFIB, has been postponed until after the 2027 general election, describing the circulating document as fake and unauthorised.

In a statement issued on Thursday by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Interior, Dr Magdalene Ajani, the ministry said its attention had been drawn to a fake press release titled “CDCFIB Recruitment Update,” dated 11th August 2026, which was falsely attributed to the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo.

According to the statement, the document, which claimed that the recruitment exercise had been deferred due to funding constraints, did not originate from the Ministry of Interior, the Minister’s office, or the CDCFIB.

“This press release is fake, unauthorised, and fraudulent. The Minister did not sign or issue this statement,” the ministry said.

It added that no decision had been made to defer the recruitment exercise until after the 2027 general election, stressing that the exercise remained ongoing.

The ministry urged members of the public and applicants to disregard the fake document in its entirety and rely solely on information published through the Ministry’s and CDCFIB’s verified platforms, including the official recruitment portal, cdcfib.gov.ng.

“Members of the public and applicants are strongly advised to disregard this document in its entirety and to rely solely on information published through the Ministry’s and CDCFIB’s verified platforms,” the statement said.

World.title: Saudi defence minister calls Iraq ‘cherished neighbour’ after strikes
World.content:
Saudi Arabia’s defence minister called Iraq a “cherished neighbour” in talks with a senior Iraqi army official on Thursday, despite last month’s deadly US-Saudi strikes on targets in the country.

The Riyadh visit was the first announced by an Iraqi security official to Saudi Arabia since Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s trip to the kingdom was cancelled after the strikes on July 29.

Officials from the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces and that includes pro-Iran groups, said the US-Saudi strikes killed 20 militants, including five Iranians.

Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming Iran-backed groups in Iraq for the attacks.

“Iraq will remain a cherished neighbour, we share bonds of brotherhood, solidarity, and mutual support with its government and its brotherly people. The Kingdom will always stand by Iraq to support its security, stability, development, and prosperity, for the benefit of Iraq and its brotherly people,” Khalid bin Salman wrote, in a post on X.

He added that he had met with director of Iraq’s Office of the Commander in Chief Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, saying the pair “reviewed Saudi-Iraqi relations in the military and defence sectors” and discussed developments in the Middle East.

“We also emphasised the importance of continued coordination and cooperation between our two countries to serve our mutual interests and ensure the region’s security and stability,” he wrote.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an alliance of Tehran-backed groups, had vowed to retaliate to the strikes, but last week announced they would postpone their response.

The first high-level meeting between Saudi Arabia and Iraq since the strikes took place last week between their foreign ministers on the sidelines of a meeting in Jordanian capital Amman.

The strikes came as Baghdad faces growing pressure from Washington to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have targeted US facilities hundreds of times during the Middle East war.

Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

AFP

World.title: Osun 2026: Deputy Senate President Urges Support for Oyebamiji, Says APC’s Victory Will Return State to Political Mainstream
World.content:
Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has urged the people of Osun State to vote for the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO), to return the state to Nigeria’s political mainstream for the development of the state.

Speaking during the grand campaign mega rally of the APC ahead of Saturday’s election at the Freedom Park, Osogbo, Osun State, on Thursday, Senator Barau said two key things are hindering the development of the state.

Senator Barau, who is the Secretary of the national campaign council of the APC for the Osun Governorship Election, said the first challenge hindering the development of the state was a lack of good leadership to lead the path for its development.

Amid a mammoth crowd that thronged the venue of the campaign rally, he said the candidate of the APC possesses the capacity to turn around the fortunes of the state for the benefit of its people.

“Osun State is a state that has enormous potential and enormous resources, both natural and human.

“But the problem is that it doesn’t have a governor to harness these resources. What is needed at this moment is to elect APC’s AMBO, who has the requisite pedigree and the requisite background to harness these resources,” he said.

He added that, “Apart from that, there’s one thing that is also lacking. Osun State is not within the mainstream of Nigerian politics. What is needed at this stage is to bring Osun State into the mainstream of Nigerian politics.

“As we speak, we have 31 states being governed by the APC. But Osun is isolated. So, you (voters) need to go out on Saturday to bring Osun into the equation of our national politics by voting for APC.

“When you do that, Osun State will gain and develop. Please, on Saturday, go out there and vote for APC’s candidate. By doing so, you have voted for development and for infrastructure.”

As a firm believer in issue-based politics and the sanctity of human life, he urged the people of the state to shun any issue capable of causing crisis before, during and after the election.

World.title: National Policing Bill: FG Extends Deadline For Submission of Memoranda, Position Papers By Eight Days
World.content:
* Submission now to close Friday, August 21

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill set up by President Bola Tinubu has extended the deadline for the submission of memoranda and position papers on the proposed legislation by eight days.

The submission of the proposed bill’s memo and position papers initially billed to close by 5pm on Thursday, August 13, 2026 will now end by Friday, August 21, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. West Africa Time (WAT).

According to a statement issued on Thursday by the Chief of Staff to the President, who also doubles as Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, the extension is intended to provide stakeholders with additional time for thorough preparation and ensure that interested individuals, institutions and organisations have adequate opportunity to make well-considered contributions to the proposed legislation.

The release stated that the Presidential Working Group is committed to ensuring that the process of developing the National Policing Bill benefits from broad consultation and the informed perspectives of Nigerians and relevant stakeholders.

The proposed legislation, Gbajabiamila further explained, is intended to provide the operational, administrative, institutional and funding framework necessary for an effective policing architecture that responds to Nigeria’s evolving security needs, while providing appropriate safeguards for accountability, professionalism and the protection of citizens’ rights.

Gbajabiamila, in the release, stated inter alia: “Given the significance of the proposed reform to the future of policing and internal security in Nigeria, the Working Group considers it important that stakeholders are afforded more opportunity to make substantive and technically sound contributions to the process.

“Accordingly, legal practitioners, civil society organisations, security sector professionals, state governments, professional bodies, academics, experts and interested members of the public are encouraged to take advantage of the extended period to submit their memoranda and position papers. All submissions must be made on or before 5:00 p.m. WAT on Friday, August 21, 2026, exclusively through the official National Policing Bill portal, nationalpolicingbill.com.

“The Working Group recognises that developing an effective policing framework requires careful consideration of critical issues, including sustainable funding, command and control structures, recruitment and training standards, operational jurisdiction, inter-agency coordination, accountability mechanisms and safeguards against political interference or abuse.

“These considerations underscore the importance of robust stakeholder engagement in developing a framework that is effective, accountable, sustainable and responsive to the peculiar security needs of communities across the Federation.

“At the conclusion of its assignment, the Presidential Working Group will present a final, implementation-ready draft of the National Policing Bill for onward legislative processing.

“The Presidential Working Group appreciates stakeholders who have already made submissions and encourages others intending to participate in this important national process to take advantage of the extension.”

Gbajabiamila had on Monday, August 3, in a bid to encourage public participation, announced an open call for memoranda and position papers from Nigerians, civil society organisations, professional bodies, security institutions and other stakeholders.

The CoS to the president, who spoke with newsmen at the end of the Group’s meeting at the State House, Abuja, disclosed that a dedicated portal, nationalpolicingbill.com, had gone live to receive submissions, with plans for migration to a government domain.

“The whole idea behind state policing is for you and I and everybody out there to take ownership. No matter your station in life, you have an opportunity to contribute meaningfully,” he said.

World.title: Katsina Moves to Block Financial Leakages, Tightens TSA Operations
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State Government has commenced moves to plug financial leakages and strengthen the implementation of the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system as part of efforts to improve accountability, transparency and efficiency in the management of the state’s public funds.

The state Commissioner for Finance, Alhaji Bello Hussaini Kagara, disclosed this Thursday at a one-day follow-up capacity-building workshop on TSA implementation organised by his ministry for accountants and initiators in the state.

He charged the accountants and other financial officers in the state to uphold high ethical standards and ensure efficient implementation of the treasury single account system.

He explained that the training was aimed at strengthening the capacity of financial officers, identifying operational gaps and improving the efficiency and transparency of the state’s financial management system.

He stressed the need for the state financial officers to identify issues surrounding payment processes, checks and balances, appropriations and the handling of payment vouchers (PVs), noting that gaps in these areas could undermine the effectiveness of the TSA system.

He explained that previous assessments had revealed instances where funds were transferred into accounts that were not intended to receive them, warning that such loopholes must be identified and addressed to safeguard government resources.

Kagara urged the participants, whom he described as critical operators of the system, to unravel challenges affecting the TSA operations and make practical recommendations that would help the state government to improve its financial management processes.

He said the state government was committed to periodic training of its financial officers to enable them update their knowledge, improve their skills and adapt to emerging developments in public financial management.

“We cannot have a perfect operation, but what we want is an efficient system. All we want to do is to ensure that we put in our best and do the best we can,” the commissioner said.

He assured the participants that recommendations arising from the workshop would be given serious consideration by the state government, adding that their contributions were important to improving the operational success of the TSA system.

The commissioner further urged the participants to demonstrate ethical competence, obedience to established procedures, self-reliance and the willingness to ask questions whenever necessary.

Kagara said the government expected the participants to translate the knowledge acquired from the training into improved performance and greater accountability in the discharge of their responsibilities.

World.title: Niger Pilgrims Board Set September 20 As Deadline For Payment of 2027 Hajj Deposits
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

The Niger State Pilgrims Welfare Board has set September 20, this year for the payment of deposits by potential 2027 Hajj pilgrims.

A statement by the Public Relations Officer of the Board, Hajia Lubabatu Mohammed Kusherki, in Minna said the deadline followed a similar action taken by the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON).

NAHCONs action, she said, is in line with a decision by the Saudi Arabia Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.

Hajia Kusherki said the Saudi authority has mandated all participating countries to upload the biodata of their intending pilgrims onto the “NUSUK MASAR platform on or before September 20, 2026, based on slots allocated to each country.

According to her, NAHCON has said that Nigeria is expected to upload details of approximately 50,000 intending pilgrim within the stipulated period.

Kusherki said the board warned that failure of intending pilgrims to register and make payment before the deadline could result in the forfeiture of allocated slots for the 2027 pilgrimage.

“The board remains committed to providing all necessary guidance and support to intending pilgrims throughout the registration process,” she stated.

Kusherki urged Intending pilgrims to visit the Niger State Pilgrims’ Welfare Board Office in Minna or designated local government centres for registration and further inquiries.

World.title: Katsina, Security Chiefs, Intensify War Against Banditry, Terrorism
World.content:
• Seek stronger collaboration to tackle scourge

Francis Sardauna in Katsina

Security chiefs, Katsina State Government and other stakeholders have called for stronger synergy, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations among security agencies to defeat terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities threatening the North-west region of the country.

The call was made at the North-west Conference of State Directors of Security, held in Katsina on Thursday, with the theme ‘Unite Against Terror.’

Speaking at the conference, the Katsina State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), Alhassan Iliyasu, said collaboration among security agencies, communities and other stakeholders to effectively tackle terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities in the region is vital.

He said the fight against terrorism and banditry could not be won by security agencies alone, stressing that every member of the society had a role to play in providing useful information and supporting security operations to tackle the region’s evolving security challenges.

He added that the conference provided an opportunity for heads of intelligence-led organisations and security agencies across the region to review emerging threats, share experiences and develop renewed strategies for curbing banditry and related criminal activities.

Iliyasu said: “The purpose of this conference is for us to come together, review the nitty-gritty of the security challenges, come up with renewed strategies and scale up our countermeasures.”

He noted that the collaboration among security agencies, community-based security structures, vigilante groups and other stakeholders would significantly improve responses to security threats across the North-west region of the country.

He commended the Director-General of the DSS, Mr Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi, for providing renewed direction for the Service and creating opportunities to strengthen its intelligence and tactical capabilities.

On his part, the Commander, 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Katsina, Brigadier-general Ishaya Ibrahim, explained that the synergy among security agencies was no longer an advantage but an imperative in confronting the evolving and borderless nature of terrorism.

He disclosed that military firepower and territorial operations alone could not defeat terrorists, adding that actionable intelligence remained critical to the success of military operations.

He said terrorists exploit gaps in information, coordination and trust, hence the need for the nation’s security agencies to bridge such gaps through real-time intelligence sharing, joint operational planning and mutual support.

In his opening remarks, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda said Katsina State had recorded significant improvements in its security challenges through a combination of both kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

Represented by his Deputy, Faruk Lawal, the governor attributed the security improvement in the state to the cooperation between conventional security agencies and the state’s home-grown security initiative, the Community Watch Corps.

He added that the state government had also “invested heavily” in non-kinetic interventions aimed at addressing some of the socio-economic factors that could fuel insecurity in the state.

He, therefore, appealed to security agencies and the media to be strategic in communicating security-related developments, warning against reports that could inadvertently amplify the activities of bandits and other criminal elements.

Radda urged the media to support security efforts by providing responsible coverage capable of boosting public confidence and the morale of security personnel operating in the North-west region of the country.

World.title: NHRC Cautions Against Hate Speech Ahead of 2027 Polls
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued a stark warning that escalating hate speech, intimidation, incitement and divisive political rhetoric could plunge Nigeria into violence and chaos ahead of the 2027 general election.

The commission said on Thursday that inflammatory statements by political and public figures were increasingly threatening human dignity, peaceful coexistence and citizens’ right to participate freely in the democratic process.

Speaking during a press conference at the NHRC headquarters in Abuja, the Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, said Nigeria must act decisively before dangerous rhetoric translates into violence.

Ojukwu specifically cited statements attributed to Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir and Senator Francis Fadahunsi, saying the commission considered some of the comments to have crossed “the red line for decency” and to have the potential to denigrate individuals or groups, deepen divisions and heighten tensions.

He stressed, however, that the intervention was not targeted at any political party, religious organisation, ethnic group or individual, but was a human-rights response designed to protect the dignity and equal worth of Nigerians.

“Freedom of expression is a fundamental human right. However, freedom of expression carries responsibilities,” Ojukwu said, warning that the right did not constitute a licence to incite violence, promote hatred, dehumanise others or deliberately provoke hostility against individuals or communities.

The NHRC boss warned that hate speech must not be dismissed as ordinary political rhetoric, arguing that language portraying people or communities as enemies, inferior, dangerous or undeserving of protection could fuel discrimination, exclusion, intimidation and violence.

According to him, the consequences could include attacks on political opponents and voters, restrictions on civic participation, displacement and insecurity, deepening ethnic and religious tensions, and a loss of public confidence in democratic institutions.

Ojukwu invoked the painful lessons of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda, noting that sustained propaganda, denigration, dehumanisation and incitement could create an environment in which discrimination and violence become increasingly acceptable.

While stressing that Nigeria was not Rwanda, he said the lesson from history was universal and should compel authorities and citizens to confront dangerous narratives before they escalated.

“The situation, if unchecked, could escalate circumstances into uncontrolled violence and chaos. God forbid,” he said.

He maintained that prevention was a fundamental human-rights obligation, adding that government had the primary responsibility under national and international law to prevent violence and protect citizens.

The commission therefore called for early identification of dangerous narratives, responsible public communication and lawful accountability for those who cross established legal boundaries.

With the 2027 elections approaching, the NHRC urged political actors to ensure that campaigns revolve around policies, programmes, competence and records of service rather than ethnic hostility, religious antagonism and personal attacks.

The commission warned that unchecked divisive rhetoric could intimidate voters, suppress political participation and trigger violence before, during and after the elections.

It also cautioned that communities that feel targeted or threatened could become vulnerable to insecurity and displacement, while prolonged political hostility could leave lasting social fractures long after the elections have ended.

Ojukwu said the protection of human rights and prevention of election-related violence must consequently be treated as complementary objectives.

The NHRC called on political parties to rein in their members and strengthen internal mechanisms for preventing and sanctioning inflammatory and intimidating rhetoric.

Religious, traditional and community leaders were similarly urged to use their influence to promote tolerance, peace and mutual respect rather than hatred, violence and division.

The commission also placed responsibility on the media, warning journalists and media organisations against becoming channels for amplifying inflammatory statements.

It urged the media to maintain professional and ethical standards and ensure that potentially harmful content was reported with context, verification and proper public-interest considerations.

Social media users and digital platforms, the commission added, must also exercise greater responsibility, particularly in verifying information before sharing material capable of provoking hostility or violence.

Law enforcement agencies were urged to respond appropriately to credible cases involving incitement, threats, intimidation and other unlawful conduct, while ensuring that investigations and prosecutions comply with the Constitution, due process and fundamental rights.

World.title: Osun Election: Fadaunsi Accuses Adeleke of Importing Violence into Osun East While Ede is Peaceful
World.content:
Alleges 30 APC members killed within a month

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Senator representing Osun East Senatorial District, Femi Fadahunsi, yesterday accused the Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, of allegedly importing political violence and terrorism into the senatorial district ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

It would be recalled that Adeleke called for arrest of Fadahunsi over reported incitement against supporters of Accord Party.

Meanwhile, Fadahunsi, who spoke at a press conference in Osogbo yesterday, alleged that more than 40 people had been killed in the district in the last one year, accusing the state government of failing to prevent the violence.

He further alleged that 30 members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) had been killed within the last month, claiming that the violence was designed to intimidate opposition supporters and prevent them from coming out to vote.

According to him, “Adeleke created terrorism from Ede into Osun East, the stronghold of APC, for us to be destabilised, so that people will not go out en masse to cast their votes.”

Fadahunsi, who chronicled several incidents of violence in Ijesa land, alleged that four people were killed while 16 others sustained gunshot injuries during the crisis over the control of local government administration.

He also referred to the violence recorded in Esa-Oke in April 2025, alleging that four people were killed while 12 others sustained gunshot wounds.

He accused unnamed government officials and political allies of being behind some of the incidents, alleging that the violence was connected to political interests in the area.

The senator further alleged that members of the Amotekun Corps killed four of his constituents in Akinlalu, leaving six others critically injured.

He said, “In the last one year, over 40 people were killed in the district unchecked by either the police or the governor.”

Fadahunsi also alleged that some individuals with links to cult groups had been used to perpetrate violence in Ijesa land.

He alleged that four people were killed in Ilesa during the local government control crisis and that several others were wounded.

The senator also referred to the death of a suspected cultist, identified as Rogba, alleging that he had been linked to previous killings before he was killed by a rival cult group.

Fadahunsi said the situation had become particularly worrisome ahead of the August 15 election, alleging that opposition supporters had been targeted.

He claimed that 12 APC members were killed within 24 hours in recent attacks, while several others sustained injuries.

“Go to Wesley Guild, there are corpses everywhere. The former Speaker, Timothy Owoeye, and Remi Omowaiye are in hospital instead of planning for the election,” he said.

He alleged that the violence was aimed at creating fear among voters in Osun East, while claiming that Ede, the governor’s home town, remained peaceful.

“We observed that it is only Osun East that this governor from Ede is terrorising,” he said.

“Adeleke created terrorism from Ede into Osun East, the stronghold of APC for us to be destabilised, so that people will not go out en masse to cast their votes.”

Fadahunsi said he had led a protest to the palace of the Owa Obokun of Ijesaland to draw attention to what he described as politically motivated killings in the area.

He urged traditional rulers and security agencies to ensure that voters were not intimidated or prevented from exercising their franchise.

“I want to urge the security agencies to ensure arrest of anyone who may want to prevent our people from coming out en masse,” he said.

The senator also accused the Director-General of the Accord Party campaign council, Senator Oyewumi Iyiola, of intervening in a case involving a suspect allegedly linked to the killing of Remi Abass in Irewole.

He questioned the justification for what he described as selective demands for justice.

“If they want to return to power by force, it is not possible. Let us do our election free and fair, not by introducing terrorism in my district to chase away the people,” Fadahunsi said.

He also dismissed allegations by Governor Adeleke against security agencies and the APC, arguing that such accusations suggested that the governor was apprehensive about the outcome of the election.

“If Governor Adeleke is accusing police, army, APC and others, then he is afraid of losing,” he said.

Fadahunsi urged residents of Osun East to remain resolute and participate in the election, assuring APC supporters that their votes would determine the outcome.

He said the APC governorship candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO), would emerge victorious in the election.

“By August 15, when all these have ended, let them be going around to be talking grammar where they feel. The people of Osun State have understood the game that they are devilish and they are ready to reject them. AMBO will win the governorship race,” he said.

World.title: Igbere Traditional Rulers Back Dep. Speaker Kalu’s Bid for Another Term, Describe His Legislative Service as Outstanding
World.content:
Igbere traditional rulers in Bende Local Government of Abia State have thrown their weight behind the 2027 bid of the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu to return to the parliament.

Speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers during Kalu’s courtesy call in the course of his “Meet Your Constituents” tour to the traditional rulers on Wednesday in Igbere, His Royal Majesty (HRM) Eze Joseph Ukaoha Anyanta applauded Kalu for his outstanding legislative service, recalling that no one before him since the return of democracy in 1999 matched his service in terms of quality representation, legislative and infrastructure records.

The traditional rulers also gave their royal blessings to the Deputy Speaker, pledging their unflinching support for his legislative deliveries.

He said: “Yours is an outstanding legislative service, the best since 1999. Yours is different and we are seeing it all over the place. We are giving you our support so that you can do your work in peace.

“Anyone who wishes you evil will not succeed. We pray to God to give you the grace to achieve your lofty dreams for Bende. Whatever we can do to make this a reality, we will do it.”

Similarly, the women, youth of Igbere and non indigenes resident in Igbere also pledged their support for the Deputy Speaker, commending him for quality representation so far.

At Ibina Hall in Onu-Ibina Igbere, the women gathered in their numbers, singing and dancing in solidarity with the Deputy Speaker’s bid.

The same was the situation at Amankalu Igbere where the non indigenes resident in the town also gave their blessings to the Deputy Speaker.

The people lauded Kalu for attracting numerous projects to Bende, noting that all the 13 electoral wards of the constituency have witnessed unprecedented improvement in roads infrastructure, construction and renovation of school building amongst other people-oriented projects.

World.title: Gayton McKenzie opens up about his sick son: ‘Prepare for the worst’
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has opened up about his son's medical issues. Images via Facebook

Gayton McKenzie has opened up his battle with a chronically ill child, who he believes was miraculously healed by answered prayer.

The Minister of Sport, Art and Culture shared the personal account in a heartfelt social media post.

GAYTON MCKENZIE SHARES POST ABOUT SICK SON

On his Facebook account, Gayton McKenzie shared a post about one of his sons, Cruz McKenzie.



The Minister and Patriotic Alliance leader shared: “This boy had so many things wrong with him medically when he was born, he was rushed to the ICU and kept there for a long time.

“We literally lived at the hospital. The doctors called me one side and said I should prepare my family for the worst.

Gayton added that his mother encouraged the family to continue praying and to ignore the doctor’s reports.



He continued: “We would pray without stopping. He was discharged and healed fully. He has never gotten sick or needed medical care again. He is a very bright teenager today, he once told me that he can get hundred percent in a test and he did it. He is a great soccer player today and such a joy.

Gayton shared that the motive for the post was to encourage parents who are going through similar circumstances.

“Prayer works, it is a joke for those that has not experience the result of prayer. Some of us fortunate enough to have experienced the power of prayer can testify from rooftops about the wonders of serving a Living and Loving God”, he added.



HOW MANY CHILDREN DOES HE HAVE?

In an interview on Morning Live in 2015, Gayton McKenzie stated that at the time, he had eight children with six women.

The PA party leader was speaking about his book titled The Uncomfortable Truth.

The memoir was written from the former convict’s experiences with love, casual sex, and relationships.



“I’ve got eight kids with six different women. Those were in my player days…in my very naughty days”, he told a surprised Leanne.

However, he added that despite the unconventional dynamic, he was not an absent father.

“Their surnames are all McKenzie; I look after all my kids.”



Gayton has remained mum about the identities of the six women who bore his eight children, one of whom is Siwelele FC owner Calvin Le John.

However, it is public knowledge that he wed his lawyer, Nicolette Joubert, in 2003.

This came after Nicolette was sent to investigate Gayton and others’ allegations of corruption at the Grootvlei Prison involving prison gangs, warders, and inmates. The exposé became international news, and Gayton was named one of the “Grootvlei Four.”



The couple had two daughters together.

A decade later, Gayton hinted that he had wronged his wife, whom he had since divorced.

He tweeted: “I hurt my ex-wife indescribably. But a bad word about me will never be heard by strangers or our kids, sheer class always.”

World.title: ‘We fear no one’ – Kaizer Chiefs star fires warning at Sundowns
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Miguel Inacio has sent a strong warning to Mamelodi Sundowns ahead of their blockbuster Betway Premiership clash at FNB Stadium on Saturday.

Amakhosi have made an impressive start to the league campaign, winning their opening two matches and building early momentum under coach Fernando Da Cruz.

Inacio, who has been a key figure in Chiefs’ defence, insists his side will not be intimidated by the reigning champions.



“We have to respect the fact that Sundowns is Sundowns, but we are also Kaizer Chiefs and we fight for our goals. We fear no one,” Inacio said.

“I think the message is clear: we fear no one, no matter if they are champions of Africa or champions of the PSL. We are going to start the game with the same ambition and fighting spirit, and win every duel.”

will also take confidence from their recent record against Sundowns, having avoided defeat in their last three meetings across all competitions.

Kaizer Chiefs ready for Sundowns

For Inacio, Saturday’s encounter also presents an opportunity to continue his strong start to the season and potentially catch the attention of the Angola national team selectors.

The defender has been out of the national team setup for several years but admits a return to the Palancas Negras is something he would welcome.

“I won’t lie, I would like to make it back to the national team, but my focus right now is Kaizer Chiefs and achieving goals with my club,” he said during a press conference at the Chiefs Village on Thursday afternoon.



“We have a lot of games and competitions ahead of us. I never think about the national team ahead of any game. The only thing on my mind right now is Leon, Tashreeq and all the Sundowns attack.

“So, that is all that I am thinking about, which is the next game for us and obviously remaining fit, training well and being prepared to be one of the options for coach Da Cruz against Sundowns.”

When do Kaizer Chiefs play Sundowns?

Kaizer Chiefs host Mamelodi Sundowns at FNB Stadium on Saturday, 15 August, with kick-off scheduled for 15:00.

The highly anticipated encounter will be televised live on SABC 1 and SuperSport 2.

World.title: SASSA payment delays leave pensioners facing lapsed policies
World.content:
Reader reaction to The South African’s report on shifting SASSA payment dates has revealed just how far the disruption reaches, touching insurance, rent, and even other grant types.

Commenter Masters Jacob shared a blunt update: their AVBOB policy has already lapsed. Funeral policies like these are a common financial priority for pensioners, often built up over years of careful payments. Also, a lapse can mean losing that cover entirely or having to restart contributions from zero, a serious blow for recipients with little room in their budgets to absorb the loss.

Rent penalties add pressure

The financial strain isn’t limited to insurance. Commenter Jaap Loggenberg detailed a direct cost tied to payment timing, noting an extra R270 charge on rent for paying after the 2nd of the month, a penalty that eats into a grant many already describe as insufficient to live on.



Furthermore, not all the fallout is directly linked to payment dates. Commenter Alvenita Calvert reported that they still have not received their child support grant, suggesting the disruption may extend beyond the Older Persons Grant to other forms of SASSA assistance.

Taken together, the comments paint a picture of a support system under strain, one where delays and shifting schedules are creating financial consequences recipients never signed up for. Also, for pensioners and grant recipients already stretched thin, the message is consistent: even small administrative changes can carry outsized costs for those with the least room to absorb them.

World.title: Former Kaizer Chiefs and Sundowns skipper retires from football
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs and Mamelodi Sundowns captain Ramahlwe Mphahlele has officially retired from professional football.

Speaking to Andile Ncube on Metro FM, Mphahele announced that he is done with playing football at the highest level.

Also read: Miguel’s warning to Sundowns: We are Kaizer Chiefs, we fear no one!



EX-KAIZER CHIEFS AND SUNDOWNS CAPTAIN RAMA MPHAHLELE RETIRES

Mphahlele had a topflight career spanning almost 20 years having first burst into the professional scenes as a teenager in 2007.

At the time, the now 36-year-old played for the now defunct Moroka Swallows until he was signed by Sundowns in 2011.

After struggling for game time in his first season at Chloorkop, Mphahlele was loaned out to AmaTuks for the 2012-13 season.



He then returned to the Brazilians with Pitso Mosimane still in charge of the team, and he later became the club’s captain.

Nonetheless, after failing to agree terms on a new contract in 2016, Mphahlele dumped Sundowns and signed for Chiefs.

He spent six seasons with the Soweto giants between 2016 and 2022 before moving to AmaZulu where he spent four seasons.



Mphahlele was also a full Bafana Bafana international with 21 caps and a single goal to his name from 2016.

Overall, he retires having made 413 topflight appearances, scored 10 goals and provided 19 assists in the process.

Also read: Bafana Bafana starlet swaps English football for MLS

World.title: ‘You’re paid to report for training’ – Ex-Downs star’s message to Saleng
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns and Orlando Pirates midfielder Benson Mhlango has asked for more clarity on the issue surrounding Monnapule Saleng.

This comes after head coach Miguek Cardoso revealed that Saleng had been separated from the squad after failing to report for a Champions League match and subsequently refusing to join the team’s training camp.

The talented winger has not featured for The Brazilians in two matches so far this season.



Mhlongo told KickOff that there could be various reasons why Saleng has not played despite Cardoso’s explanation.

“Saleng’s issue is confusing because nobody is coming out to reveal the real issue,” he said.

“We don’t know if it has to do with money or personal issues.



“The last time at Pirates, his issue was money, so this time… maybe he is one of the boys who don’t want to sit on the bench.

“Nobody knows the truth. Sundowns is an institution that believes in playing in a certain system; players must fit in.

“Flemming Berg [the club’s sporting director) was brought to Sundowns to implement that system.”



Saleng left out in the cold

Before leaving Orlando Pirates in January, Saleng had not kicked a ball for the Buccaneers in over a year. He urged the ex-Bucs star to show up for training.

“My message to all the players is, remember you are not only paid to play a match, but you are also paid to report for training.

“You are paid to be a team player. Some players get to start, some sit on the bench, and some watch from the stands,” Mhlongo added.



With Sundowns possessing depth in attacking areas, Saleng’s chances of playing are slim and he might need to impress everytime he is given an opportunity.

The ex-Bafana midfielder feels sometimes players can join a club at the wrong time.

“When you join Sundowns, you must first evaluate if you are better than the players they already have.



“If I had joined Pirates in the days of Old-John Mabizela, there was no way I was going to play because Mabizela was in form.

“It all comes down to timing,” Mhlongo explained.

Will Saleng find his way back into the team?

“For instance, if you go to Sundowns now to play as a right-back, you are taking chances because you are definitely competing against Khuliso Mudau.



“Some agents are not honest with their players; they are just chasing transactions.

“It is vital for players to understand the hierarchy and the level of performance required to displace an incumbent starter.”

What’s your take on the whole issue?

World.title: Ramokgopa defends Eskom unbundling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The electricity minister, Kgosientsho Ramokgopa, has once again defended the restructuring of Eskom.

Recently, the National Union of Mineworkers said workers had not been properly consulted, and the plan would result in higher electricity prices and the loss of jobs.

But Ramakgopa said the opposite is true. He said the unbundling of the transmission company would mean greater investments and in theory can result into price reduction.

"So, the issue of unbundling is not the issue, the question is the pace and scale...The technical team will continue to feed into that process. It's unfolding," he said.

The intention to restructure Eskom was first pronounced in the 2019 State of the Nation Address where the process to transform the structure of the country's electricity industry to better serve the needs of the country was outlined.

The restructure meant that Eskom would be split into three separate entities including Generation, Transmission and Distribution.

All of which would still remain under Eskom Holdings.

Two months ago, Ramaphosa confirmed that the Eskom Restructuring Task Team established at the beginning of March 2026 had made progress towards the establishment of an independent transmission system operator.

World.title: No evidence to prove suspects linked to illegal mining
World.content:
RUSTENBURG - There’s nothing to prove that the eight survivors of the Nkaneng mine dump tragedy were illegal miners.



Instead, two Basotho nationals appeared in the Rustenburg Magistrate’s Court on immigration charges.



Two others were released because their documents remain valid until September.



The men were injured when rubble collapsed at a mine dump in Marikana, burying them.



Fourteen others died.



Like many illegal mining cases, this one went nowhere.



The state failed to prosecute suspected illegal miners for lack of evidence.



Illegal mining is a massive economic, structural, and humanitarian crisis in South Africa.



The country loses an estimated R60 billion to R70 billion a year to illegal mining but new proposed legislation aims to criminalise illegal mining operations, offering hope for change.



Under the new laws, offenders could face up to 30 years in prison and fines of up to R100 million.



eNCA's Bafedile Moerane reports in the video above.

World.title: He lured them with modelling dreams — now social media rapist jailed for life
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A 26-year-old rapist who lured women through social media under the pretext of modelling, promotional, and photoshoot opportunities will spend life behind bars.

The High Court in Johannesburg sentenced Victor Mokoena four life terms for raping four women.

Mokoena was also sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment for robbery with aggravating circumstances, two years for assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm and one year for pointing an object resembling a firearm.

The man who hides behind social media

Mokoena's modus operandi remained consistent with his victims, using a different name but targeting them on social media.

The National Prosecuting Authority's Magaboke Mohlatlole said Mokoena operated in and around Johannesburg, targeting young women through Facebook and Instagram.

“He presented himself as a photographer or promoter and lured his victims with offers of modelling, promotional and photoshoot opportunities. Once the victims arrived at the agreed locations, Mokoena took them to secluded areas, where he raped and assaulted them,” Mohlatlole said.

Investigations end Mokeona's raping spree

Mokoena committed the crime between March 2021 and October 2024, under the raider

“He deleted conversations and contact details from the victims’ cellphones in an apparent attempt to conceal his identity and frustrate the investigation,” Mohlatlole said.

Mohlatlole said it was not until the investigation linked several cases through the similarities in Mokoena’s modus operandi and digital evidence obtained from the victims.

'Treated victim with disdain'

He said the court concurred with the State’s submissions and found that Mokoena had treated his victims with disdain and had used derogatory language towards them.

This saw the court hand down the hefty sentence.

Robbery with aggravating circumstances, assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm, and pointing an object resembling firearm counts are to run concurrently with the life sentences.

The NPA welcomed the sentence, saying it reiterates its commitment to pursuing perpetrators of sexual offences and ensuring that victims of gender-based violence receive justice

World.title: Mapisa-Nqakula to ask court to declare her not guilty
World.content:
PRETORIA - Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula plans to ask the court to dismiss the corruption and money laundering charges against her.



Her lawyers told the High Court in Pretoria that she will apply for discharge her under Section 174 of the Criminal Procedure Act.



The former defence minister faces twelve counts of corruption and one of money laundering.



The case involves allegations that defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlhovu paid her R4.5 million in bribes.

On Thursday, the state closed its case, leaving Mapisa-Nqakula to decide whether to present her defence.



Meanwhile, the court has ruled in favour of eNCA and the SABC, allowing the media to broadcast proceedings going forward.



eNCA’s Moloko Moloto has the story in the video above.

World.title: ‘This is their time to shine’: Mantwa Chinoamadi on women leading Standard Bank Joy of Jazz
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – For nearly four decades, Mantwa Chinoamadi has been one of the quiet powerhouses behind South Africa’s live music scene.

As the producer of the Standard Bank Joy of Jazz, she has helped shape what is now one of the continent’s biggest jazz festivals.

This year, as the event marks its 25th anniversary, Chinoamadi said the industry is finally shifting – and women are leading the sound.

From intern to industry leader

Chinoamadi’s career started in the late 1980s at T Music Man. She was an intern, and the only woman in the room.

“It was quite difficult because I was the only woman and a lot of the men were saying ‘what is this girl doing here?’ But I knew what I was doing,” she said.

That determination was rooted early.

“My father always said I do not want girls or boys. I want strong human beings who will go out there and get whatever they want.”

She has been involved with Standard Bank Joy of Jazz since 1999, and has watched the festival, and the industry, evolve.

Changing the narrative, on stage and off

For years, Chinoamadi said, the story of South African jazz put men at the front and women in the background. She set out to change that.

“We knew we wanted to change the narrative. For too long the front stage belonged to the men and the women were just backing singers. This is their time to shine,” she said.

Now she’s seeing the results.

“It’s been quite encouraging to see... we are getting a lot of young women who are also coming into the fold. So that gives us great comfort,” she said.

Behind the scenes, Chinoamadi is also breaking ground.

“This was the first time we've had all women working on the production, which was also quite exciting for us because we're also giving opportunities to women,” she said.

25 years of Joy

The Standard Bank Joy of Jazz returns to the Sandton Convention Centre on 25 and 26 September 2026.

The festival will also host a free concert on Heritage Day, 24 September, though tickets for that event are already sold out.

As the festival celebrates a quarter-century, Chinoamadi says the goal remains the same: bring joy to fans and create space for the next generation.
