World.title: Eesti Pank to issue Hiiumaa‑themed €2 coin
World.content:
The central motif of the coin is Hiiumaa's landmark, the Kõpu Lighthouse, surrounded by sea waves, with the light beams reflecting the striped pattern of Hiiumaa's traditional folk skirt. This pattern is an important part of the island's identity, symbolizing continuity and resilience, and representing the security of the home island.

The design is by Kaupo Kangro.

The Kõpu Lighthouse was completed in its original form in 1531 and is the third‑oldest operating lighthouse in the world.

One million coins dedicated to Hiiumaa will be minted and released into circulation through retail channels. The coin will be valid as official legal tender throughout the euro area.

Hiiumaa, known for its distinctive nature and long maritime history, will open Eesti Pank's new coin series dedicated to Estonia's counties. The aim of the series is to highlight the diversity and cultural uniqueness of Estonia's regions.

World.title: Economy minister rejects proposed restrictions on nicotine products
World.content:
Economy Minister Erkki Keldo declined to approve a draft bill aimed at curbing the use of nicotine products among young people as the proposed changes could have a significant impact on sellers and importers.

The restrictions proposed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Justice would allow nicotine pouches, nicotine strips and nicotine sprays containing no more than four milligrams of nicotine per gram to be sold in Estonia. The aim is to reduce the use of nicotine products among young people.

Erkki Keldo sent a letter to the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs on Wednesday informing it that he had declined to approve the draft bill. Keldo said the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications supports protecting the health of children and young people and curbing the illegal sale of nicotine products, but considers it important that measures restricting freedom of enterprise be sufficiently justified and proportionate.

Snus. Source: Flickr

"The changes proposed in the draft bill could significantly affect manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers of nicotine products operating in Estonia. The explanatory memorandum does not adequately assess the extent of these impacts or provide a convincing justification for the proposed maximum nicotine content of 4 mg/g for nicotine-containing products related to tobacco products," Keldo said.

He noted that the draft bill's maximum nicotine content of four milligrams per gram is based on Latvia's approach, but said this was not sufficient justification for restricting freedom of enterprise.

"The explanatory memorandum does not indicate the nicotine content of nicotine pouches and other products covered by the bill currently on the Estonian market, what proportion of products currently marketed legally would comply with the proposed limit or how many businesses and products would be affected by the change," the economy minister said.

He is also dissatisfied that the draft bill does not include a comparative analysis of approaches taken by other EU member states or explain why Latvia's regulations are the best model for Estonia.

Keldo said the explanatory memorandum needs to be supplemented with a comparison of different options. The impact of the limit on the health of children and young people, the risk of accidental poisoning, businesses, the functioning of the legal market and consumer behavior should also be analyzed.

The data presented in the explanatory memorandum concern products containing e-cigarette liquid, but does not address the impact of the changes on nicotine pouches, strips, sprays and heated nicotine sticks.

"We ask that the impact assessment be expanded to separately cover all product categories regulated by the draft bill and the requirements proposed for them," the minister said.

Keldo also wants the impact of the changes on Estonian manufacturers, exports, employment and regional businesses to be examined, along with their impact on the legal market, illegal trade and tax revenue.

"Possible substitution behavior must also be analyzed, including whether some consumers could switch to products with unregulated contents or to other tobacco and nicotine products and what impact this could have on achieving the draft bill's public health objective," Keldo said.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is also dissatisfied with a provision in the draft bill stipulating that products may not contain substances that produce a flavor or aroma other than tobacco or menthol and that only substances listed in a specific regulation may be used to provide those flavors. However, the explanatory memorandum does not explain why those particular substances are considered suitable or what costs businesses could incur in reformulating existing products.

Keldo said the bill's relationship with the planned update of the European Union's legal framework for tobacco and nicotine products should also be assessed.

The Ministry of Social Affairs has previously said that people are starting to use nicotine products at increasingly younger ages. While young people previously tried nicotine at ages 15 or 16, they are now doing so at around age 11. Nicotine pouches and e-cigarettes are the most common products used by those starting out.

Estonia's so-called Superministry building housing several government ministries. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Just over one-fifth of the nicotine products currently on the market comply with the requirements proposed in the draft bill. Around 60 percent of products would have to be reformulated, while nearly one-fifth would have to be removed from the market.

Several European countries have tightened restrictions on nicotine products in recent years. Latvia raised the minimum age for purchasing tobacco and nicotine products to 20 two years ago. No such proposal is currently under consideration in Estonia.

The new rules are planned to take effect in 2028, although the exact date will be determined as the draft bill moves through the legislative process.

World.title: Baltics' first AI factory to open in Estonia
World.content:
Dutch cloud company Nebius' Tallinn AI factory will begin operating at Greenergy Data Centers' data center this year. With a capacity of 22 megawatts, it will be the largest in the Baltics.

Nasdaq-listed Nebius announced Wednesday that it signed agreements in the second quarter to expand the company's AI infrastructure network in Europe. The first phase of its Tallinn AI factory, with a capacity of 22 megawatts, is expected to begin operating later this year.

Nebius Head of Communications Tom Blackwell said Estonia was a natural choice for the company thanks to its world-class engineers, vibrant digital economy and startup culture, as well as its ambitious plans for both artificial intelligence and the transition to clean energy.

"Nebius' Tallinn AI factory, which is being developed in partnership with Greenergy Data Centers, will provide state-of-the-art infrastructure to support Estonia's growing innovation ecosystem and help accelerate the development and adoption of artificial intelligence," he said.

Nebius' global capacity network has expanded rapidly. In Europe, the company is developing large-scale AI factories in Lappeenranta, Finland, and Béthune, France. It also has an operating center in Mäntsälä, Finland, as well as AI infrastructure projects in the United Kingdom, Spain and Iceland. Nebius' major customers include Microsoft and Meta.

Greenergy Data Centers CEO Kert Evert said Nebius' decision to choose Greenergy shows that Estonia is emerging as a competitive destination for large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Blackwell said Nebius wants to work closely with the Estonian government, businesses and universities to develop AI skills, broaden access to artificial intelligence capabilities and strengthen Estonia's position as a leading hub for AI innovation.

Martin Salo, co-founder of Tensor Estate, a group of Estonian entrepreneurs that became a shareholder in Greenergy Data Centers last month, said the newly announced project is the first phase of a larger development that will make Estonia one of the international hubs for AI infrastructure in the coming years.

"Until now, Northern Europe's major AI factories have been concentrated primarily in Finland, Sweden and Norway, thanks to favorable electricity prices, renewable energy and a suitable climate. Having the Baltics' first AI factory come here means Estonia is joining the club of countries where the world's leading AI companies are building their infrastructure," Salo said.

In late July, Greenergy Data Centers' Head of Hyperscale Martin Rungi told ERR that attracting one major international customer to Estonia would make it significantly easier for data centers to secure additional customers, as the market develops after the first breakthrough.

In Nebius' case, however, the question of its ties to Russian technology company Yandex cannot be overlooked, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and changed its name to Nebius Group, which is headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is also a co-founder of Yandex, but has since renounced his Russian citizenship.

A Greenergy representative said last month that such labeling was inappropriate, arguing that Nebius is probably one of the most thoroughly vetted organizations, given that despite its former ties to Russia, it has earned the trust of Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, the U.S. government and the New York Stock Exchange.

Economy minister: We have consulted security agencies

As government agencies have had concerns about Nebius and the workforce at the AI factory set to operate in Hüüru, Estonian security agencies have been consulted, Minister of Economic Affairs and Industry Erkki Keldo said.

"On the one hand, cutting-edge investments like these /.../ are certainly very welcome in Estonia, but on the other hand, the government has an obligation to look at the broader security picture. So yes, we are aware of the background, we are also in contact with Estonian authorities and will certainly minimize the risks," he said, adding that it is very important to understand that the factory is purely a private investment.

If questions arise about a company's background or workforce, there are rules and security agencies in place, and those agencies have also informed the public about potential risks and threats, the minister noted.

"We certainly have to ensure that any sensitive data, sensitive sectors and sensitive technologies do not, for example, fall into the hands of high-risk countries. And when using different types of data, we have to pay attention to whose technology we are using and where we use and store data, to ensure that it is protected. That is certainly what we are doing," Keldo said.

According to Keldo, Nebius was also discussed at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday and discussions on the matter will continue in the coming weeks.

"Estonian businesses need to understand these potential risks, including the company itself and that people with Russian backgrounds and Russian contacts are not welcomed here with overly open arms. We are certainly somewhat more vigilant about this than perhaps other European countries are, and that will remain the case in the future," Keldo said.

The article was updated to add comments from Minister Erkki Keldo.

World.title: Baghdad and Erbil agree on unified digital customs system across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Baghdad and Erbil have agreed to fully adopt the digital ASYCUDA customs system across border crossings, with non-oil border earnings shared equally by the federal and Kurdistan regional governments.

The deal is a significant step toward standardizing customs processes across Iraq and addressing long-standing disagreements over border revenues and claimed import quantities.

ASYCUDA, designed by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), digitizes customs declarations, payments, and clearing processes, allowing authorities to better monitor products entering the nation and the income they earn.

Linking customs operations to Iraq’s banking and electronic payment systems may help limit the potential for underreporting, revenue leakage, and corruption at border crossings.

The deal comes as Iraq’s Finance Ministry and Central Bank work to digitize customs, payments, and government financial data in collaboration with UNCTAD.

A combined computerized customs system for Baghdad and Erbil might give more accurate revenue data while resolving one of the two governments’ ongoing financial issues.

The change is also significant for Iraq’s overall economy.

More open and uniform customs processes might facilitate cross-border commerce, boost governmental revenues, and enhance the business climate as Iraq pursues more foreign investment and closer integration with international markets.

World.title: Iraq’s Chief Justice Faiq Zidan meets Syrian President Al-Sharaa in Damascus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Thursday, marking another high-level Iraqi outreach to a neighboring Arab state as Baghdad seeks to bolster regional relations under rising security problems.

Al-Sharaa welcomed Zidan and an Iraqi delegation to the People’s Palace, which also included Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Justice Minister Mazhar al-Wais.

According to the Syrian president, the talks focused on extending judicial and legal cooperation between Iraq and Syria, as well as resolving mutual concerns.

The visit also resulted in more practical conversations among the two nations’ judicial officials. Iraqi and Syrian authorities agreed to set up joint judicial committees to continue working on cases involving Syrian prisoners and other cross-border legal issues.

Zidan’s visit is crucial as he is one of the most prominent persons in Iraq’s state institutions, and it coincides with Baghdad’s increased diplomatic, security, and judicial interaction with its neighbors.

The Damascus meetings come after a separate Iraqi security group visited Riyadh, where senior military official Abdul Amir al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman.

Zidan had also just visited Ankara as part of a larger Iraqi effort to build ties with Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey.

That approach has become more urgent in light of the regional escalation involving Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

In late July, the United States and Saudi Arabia conducted synchronized attacks against locations used by Iran-aligned organizations in Iraq, after Riyadh accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones against Saudi energy infrastructure.

The incident put Baghdad under strong pressure to prevent armed organizations from exploiting Iraqi territory to launch assaults on neighboring nations and also highlighted the potential that militia activity may harm Iraq’s improved ties with Arab governments.

Against this setting, Zidan’s encounter with Al-Sharaa is significant beyond regular court cooperation.

Iraq and Syria share a long border and confront shared concerns such as terrorism, organized crime, prisoners, and cross-border security. Baghdad also has a strategic interest in preserving stable ties with Damascus, as Iraq strives to boost regional connections and prevent unrest from spilling over its borders.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration sees recent diplomatic efforts as part of a larger effort to strengthen Iraq’s ties with its neighbors while keeping the nation out of the developing conflict between Iran and its regional adversaries.

Baghdad has increasingly emphasized that choices on security, armament, and relations with neighboring governments must be made by Iraqi official authorities rather than armed groupings.

The travels to Damascus and Riyadh therefore convey an essential message: although Iran-aligned militias have exacerbated tensions between Iraq and certain of its neighbors, Iraqi official institutions are working directly with those nations to restore cooperation and avoid further escalation.

Strengthening judicial, diplomatic, and security ties with Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey might serve as an essential regional buffer for Iraq as it seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, control armed groups, and avoid being drawn further into the region’s crises.

World.title: Iraq’s Al-Shammari visits Riyadh to meet Saudi Defense Minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A top Iraqi security team has traveled to Riyadh for meetings with Saudi Arabia’s leadership, as Baghdad and the Kingdom work to improve security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

First Lieutenant General Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman on Thursday to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

According to reports from the visit, the conversations included cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration.

The conference is especially significant in light of the combined US-Saudi attacks on Iran-linked militia locations in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

The strikes drastically escalated tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, highlighting the Iraqi government’s problems in preventing armed groups from exploiting its territory to target neighboring nations.

Thursday’s visit indicates that both parties are now attempting to move beyond that conflict via direct military and intelligence collaboration.

Prince Khalid underlined Saudi Arabia’s commitment to Iraq’s security, stability, and economic growth, identifying it as an essential neighbor with whom the Kingdom has strong political and social relations.

The meetings in Riyadh follow Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali al-Humaidan’s visit to Baghdad last week, during which he met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and reiterated an offer for the Iraqi leader to visit Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad’s security cooperation with Riyadh has grown more vital as the government seeks to prevent Iran-backed militias from drawing Iraq into a larger regional conflict.

Al-Zaidi has frequently said that Iraqi soil should not be used to attack other nations and has stepped up efforts for weaponry to be put solely under state control.

The most recent Iraqi trip to Riyadh symbolizes more than just normal defense diplomacy. It is part of a joint effort by Baghdad and Saudi Arabia to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into conflict.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: Iraq sets September 30 for US-led coalition exit as Al-Zaidi turns focus to Iran-linked militia weapons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has reaffirmed Sept. 30 as the end date for the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, putting more pressure on Baghdad to confront what could be the most difficult aspect of its sovereignty agenda: bringing weapons held by powerful Iran-aligned factions under state control.

During a meeting with U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) Commander Admiral Brad Cooper, Al-Zaidi said that October 1 will signal the beginning of a “new phase” for Iraq in the absence of a foreign coalition military presence.

The Prime Minister again emphasized the importance of the Iraqi state having exclusive control over weaponry, citing sovereignty, security, and economic growth.

Iraqi authorities said plans are already beginning to hand over remaining coalition locations, notably those in northern Iraq, to Iraqi security forces before the deadline.

The timeline is based on a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington to end the coalition mission and transition the US-Iraq security partnership to direct bilateral cooperation.

However, the departure eliminates one of the primary justifications used by Iran-backed militias to preserve their weapons and strike US objectives.

Several prominent Iran-aligned factions work inside or alongside the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), who are officially part of Iraq’s governmental security system.

The PMF is made up of various groups with varying political and ideological perspectives, and it should not be viewed as a unified bloc.

However, organizations like Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and other Iran-aligned militias have maintained strong ties with Tehran and have rejected calls to relinquish their weapons.

Their actions have become an increasingly severe issue for Al-Zaidi’s administration.

Recent strikes ascribed by neighboring governments to Iran-backed forces operating from Iraqi soil have jeopardized Baghdad’s improved ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab countries, as well as led to foreign military intervention in Iraq.

The escalation has put Baghdad in a difficult position: denouncing breaches of Iraqi sovereignty while also facing demands from its neighbors to prohibit armed groups from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten them.

For Al-Zaidi, the September 30 withdrawal may fundamentally alter that equation.

Once the coalition mission is over, Iran-aligned elements will find it more difficult to justify maintaining autonomous military capabilities by citing the presence of foreign soldiers.

Baghdad will then have to decide whether it can impose its notion of a single armed authority in Iraq.

That problem is especially critical since Al-Zaidi is aiming to shift Iraq’s focus from decades of war and proxy conflict to rebuilding, investment, and closer economic ties with the US, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, and other foreign allies.

Repeated militia assaults risk undercutting that plan by raising investor anxiety and subjecting Iraq to reprisal for military choices that its government claims were not authorized.

The coalition’s exit therefore means more than just the removal of foreign troops.

It might serve as the catalyst for a far wider debate over who eventually controls Iraq’s armaments and war-making choices.

Baghdad will find it easy to declare complete sovereignty on October 1.

Demonstrating it will be far more difficult.

If Al-Zaidi is serious about guaranteeing that no foreign military presence stays in Iraq, the same sovereignty concept will increasingly be expected to apply to armed forces whose allegiance, weapons, or choices are not under the control of the Iraqi state.

Bringing such weapons under state control might prove to be one of the most important—and difficult—tests of Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

JAMMU: Thirty-five years after an explosion rocked Jammu Tawi railway station, killing three people and leaving 18 others wounded, Govt Railway Police (GRP) Jammu Thursday claimed it arrested Altaf Hussain Sheikh, a fugitive terrorist wanted in the case.A native of Marhama, Bijbehara, in south Kashmirâs Anantnag district, Sheikh went underground after the April 2, 1991, attack along with two co-accused even as their accomplice, Aman Ullah Khan, was caught that day. Charged under relevant provisions of the stringent Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, Explosive Substances Act, and Ranbir Penal Code, Sheikh managed to evade arrest for three-and-a-half decades by concealing his identity and assuming another, a GRP spokesperson said.During the investigation, the fugitive terrorists were declared âabscondersâ by court. âIn the past two years, GRP Jammu intensified the hunt for the trio. A team verified Sheikhâs identity by examining his residential details and other particulars and found that he had established himself as a successful businessman in Bijbehara,â the spokesperson said.Sheikh was produced before the TADA court Thursday for further legal proceedings, the spokesperson added.

NEW DELHI: The Govt of NCT of Delhi has notified 20% horizontal reservation for ex-Agniveers in direct recruitment to the posts of warder and matron in the prison department.The 20% quota he has been provided by the Delhi Lieutenant Governor (LG) in exercise of powers conferred by the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution of India, read with the relevant recruitment rules governing the posts of warder and matron in the Delhi prison department. World.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the countryâs ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).

Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIMâs goals.

The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.

Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, âAs against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.





The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.

Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.

World.title: 'Majority of students innocent': BCI reverses ban on NALSAR 2026 batch over CJI invite row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday modified its controversial circular that had effectively barred graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law's 2026 batch from enrolling as advocates.

In a fresh communication, released hours after the original decision, the BCI clarified that 2026 graduates of the university would be "entitled to seek enrolment with any state bar council of their choice".

"After thorough discussion, the members are of the unanimous view that as per the latest report, vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass out students) are innocent and they were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect," the BCI statement said.

"It has further been reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating the inncoent student," the BCI said.

"No student shall be made to suffer without any fault on his part," it added.

The latest development came hours after the legal regulator triggered widespread criticism by directing all state bar councils not to enrol any student graduating from NALSAR in 2026 until further orders.





The earlier circular was issued after a section of graduating students at the premier law university objected to a reported proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at the institution's convocation.

"No student who has obtained a law degree from NALSAR University of Law in the year 2026 shall be enrolled as an advocate until further directions are issued by the Bar Council of India," the order had said.

The regulator had also sought a detailed report from the university within three days, asking it to identify students who had allegedly initiated, organised or mobilised the campaign against the proposed participation of the Chief Justice.

In a strongly-worded statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra had said students who did not show respect for the country's highest judicial office could not be expected to become responsible members of the legal profession.

World.title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
World.content:
Nepali PM Balen Shah had raised up the issue of border with India, including Lipulekh.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.âThe Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives. But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,â Khanal said.He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era. Shah said Nepal had found that ânot only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.âIndia rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said âthere is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.â He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land. India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as âneither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. âThe issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Personsâ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. âWe have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,â Gyawali had said. âWe are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.âKhanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements. He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.âUnder the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,â Khanal said.He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.

World.title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Dalit politics in

is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. Not any more. Mayawatiâs BSP today is a much weaker force.

The last three elections in the state have pushed Mayawati, the four-time chief minister of UP, to the margins of state politics. This has opened up the Dalit space and triggered an interesting scramble among political parties for a slice of the Dalit pie in the 2027 assembly elections.

So, we have the BJP playing the name-change game in Bhadohi and organising a 7-month campaign to honour 15th-century saint-poet Sant Ravi Das. Then we have Samajwadi Party chief

announcing 14 extra seats for the Dalits to cement his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) politics.

Congress too is trying to win back voters it lost decades ago. Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, who is trying to consolidate his own space in the state.

As Uttar Pradesh heads towards 2027, the question is: if the BSP continues to lose ground, where does Mayawatiâs old support base go and which of her rivals stands to gain the most?

From 206 seats to one: How BSP lost ground

The BSPâs rise in UP politics was as dramatic as its fall. The party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 with the idea of giving Dalits and other marginalized communities an independent voice.





Mayawati, who emerged as his political successor, took the BSP to great heights in Uttar Pradesh. Under her leadership, the BSP won a majority on its own in the 2007 assembly elections, winning 206 seats with a vote share of 30.43%.

Dalits, who constitute around 21% of UPâs population as per the 2021 census, have for years been the core base of Mayawatiâs Bahujan Samaj Party. But that dynamic has now changed.

BSP is a much weaker force today. Mayawati has failed to mobilise Dalit support for her BSP in the last two elections in the state, thereby opening up the space for other political contenders.

In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawatiâs dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her partyâs vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSPâs influence among Dalits.

As Mayawati gears up for the 2027 assembly challenge, she faces an uphill road. The BSP chief has not just lost support of voters, but also control over her party. So, when Mayawati issued a stern message that all the candidates for the upcoming poll will be finalised by her and not by her nephew Akash Anand, it was an indication of the internal tussle in her party.

Akash Anand, who has been in and out of Mayawatiâs favour in the past, launched the partyâs 2027 assembly poll campaign from Sadabad in Hathras this week.

Mayawati, who has often been accused of helping the BJP, has ruled out any pre-poll alliance. She has claimed that some candidates have already been finalised for the upcoming assembly elections. Mayawati has asked party cadres to start rebuilding the party and drum up OBC support ahead of the polls. The cadres have apparently been asked to remind people of the party's past governance and convince them that the real benefit and welfare of the OBC community lie with the BSP and its "iron lady government".

Mayawati, however, must consider that it will be difficult for the BSP to come back to power only by holding on to its core Dalit vote alone. It will have to recreate the Dalit-OBC combination that originally carried Mayawati to power in Lucknow with a majority of her own.

BJP's Dalit outreach gets sharper ahead of 2027

One interesting fallout of BSPâs decline has been the BJPâs aggressive outreach to woo the Dalits. When Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar last month, he put the BJP right at the middle of the Dalit outreach battle ahead of 2027 polls.

The move also revived an old political contest over name-change politics. Mayawati was the one who had renamed Bhadohi as Sant Ravidas Nagar in December 1997. Akhilesh Yadav restored the old name in 2014. Now, by bringing Sant Ravidas Nagar back, Yogi sought to make a bigger political point, accusing the SP of erasing a Dalit symbol while positioning the BJP as a party willing to restore it.

Mayawati publicly welcomed the decision, a rare moment of agreement with the ruling party.

She was quick, however, to remind voters that it was her government that had changed the district's name in the first place and that the decision was later reversed under Akhilesh.

The party realises that Dalit votes are up for grabs and hence is going all out to woo them. The partyâs 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyanâ appears planned to coincide with assembly elections in two key states, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, early next year.

Both these states have a sizeable population of Dalits who play an important role in many constituencies. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Soneylal) together bagged 63 Scheduled Caste (SC) seats compared to 20 won by the then Samajwadi Party-led opposition alliance. But the 2024 Lok Sabha polls changed the dynamics, with the SP and the Congress winning 43 of the 80 seats in the state and pushing the BJP to make an aggressive outreach.

The loss of Faizabad seat to SP's Awadhesh Prasad, a Pasi leader, was particularly significant and gave Akhilesh Yadav fresh ammunition for his PDA pitch.

Earlier this year, the Yogi Adityanath government approved the âDr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojna" under which Rs 1 crore is to be allocated to each of the state's 403 assembly constituencies for the beautification and development of statues of social reformers.

The BJP's efforts to woo Dalits has also been visible in its recent Cabinet expansion. Of the six new ministers inducted into the Yogi government, two were Dalits, Krishna Paswan from the Pasi community and Surendra Singh Daler from the Valmiki community. Three others were from OBC groups. Two non-Yadav OBC ministers were also given independent charge.

The BJP's primary task ahead of 2027 would be to hold on to the non-Jatav Dalit support it built over the past decade and prevent a repeat of 2024.

SPâs Dalit outreach

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also showed that the Dalits in UP were ready to back other political parties who wooed them. Dalit support played a key role in the spectacular success of Akhilesh Yadavâs Samajwadi Party, which won 37 seats in 2024.

Together with its alliance partner Congress, the INDIA bloc won 43 of the 80 seats in the state, pushing the BJP on the back foot. Akhilesh Yadav, who has centred his politics around PDA (Pichhde, Dalits and Aplasankhyaks), gained from his Dalit outreach in the 2024 elections.

His Samajwadi Party fielded two Dalit candidates from general seats. While one of them went on to win the all-important Faizabad seat, the other lost by just 10,585 votes to the BJP in Meerut.

How Samajwadi Party performed when they contested independently

Little wonder, in the run-up to the 2027 assembly elections, Akhilesh has already announced plans to field 14 Dalit candidates from general seats. Uttar Pradesh has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and two for Scheduled Tribes.

With 14 more candidates on general seats, the total tally of reserved candidates for SP will increase to 100. This will help reinforce his message to the Dalits in line with his PDA politics.

The move will also help the SP shed the narrative of being a Muslim-Yadav party.

Congress tries to reclaim lost ground

has made it clear that Dalits would now play a 'central role' in Congress. Before Mayawati and the BSP built their massive Dalit vote bank in the 1990s, Congress was the primary choice for Uttar Pradesh's Dalits.

For nearly three decades after that, Congress was almost pushed out of UP politics.

Rahul Gandhi has started his road to the UP election by acknowledging that the party had failed to take the right steps for the community in the 1980s and 1990s. He even praised Kanshi Ram for bringing Dalits together and giving the community a sense of confidence.

Rahul has also made the Constitution a regular part of his social justice pitch.

He is often seen carrying the red book of the Constitution while warning that constitutional rights and reservation are under threat. He has repeatedly invoked BR Ambedkar in the same pitch, asserting that Congress wants to position itself as a guardian of the Constitution.

The party has also put a Dalit leader in charge of Uttar Pradesh. Rajendra Pal Gautam, who heads the Congressâs Scheduled Castes Department, has been appointed UP in-charge ahead of the 2027 polls.

Interestingly, Gautam had also made an unsuccessful attempt to meet Mayawati at her Lucknow residence earlier this year.

Whether the party will be able to translate this outreach into votes remains to be seen.

Chandrashekhar Azad adds another claimant

Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, whose 2024 victory from Nagina made him a prominent figure in UPâs Dalit politics. Unlike BJP, SP or Congress, Azad is trying to build an independent space outside the BSP. His challenge now is to take that appeal beyond one constituency and build an organisation strong enough to matter across the state in 2027.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

That is what makes the coming assembly election in Uttar Pradesh interesting. For decades, politics in Uttar Pradesh has revolved around caste. Political parties build their electoral strategies around social coalitions, loyalty of communities and traditional vote base.

Mayawati may no longer command the Dalit vote the way she once did, but that vote bank has not disappeared. It simply has more claimants. And in 2027, where those voters eventually move could make a significant difference.

World.title: Six workers dead, 14 injured as water, debris enter tunnel in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli
World.content:
At least six people died and 14 others sustained injuries on Thursday (August 13, 2026) after water and debris entered a tunnel under construction at a hydroelectric project site in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand, officials said.

According to preliminary information shared by the officials, 22 workers were trapped inside the tunnel. Twenty people have been brought out of the tunnel. Of them, six were declared dead, while 14 others have sustained injuries and are undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital. Information about the remaining two workers was not immediately available.

Earlier, officials said 16 workers were rescued after water and debris entered the under-construction tunnel in the Pipalkoti area of Chamoli.

According to the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the incident was reported around 7.05 p.m. Preliminary information suggested that 22 workers were inside the tunnel being built for a Tehri Hydro Development Corporation Limited (THDC) project when water and debris entered it.

Rescue operations were launched soon after the incident was reported. Teams from the Indian Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and SDRF were rushed to the site and raced against time to locate and evacuate the trapped workers.

District-level rescue teams, the local police and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel were also involved in the operation.

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed concern over the incident and directed officials to carry out the rescue operation on a war footing. He said the government’s priority was to ensure the safe evacuation of every worker trapped inside the tunnel.

Chamoli district has witnessed heavy rainfall over the past several days. On Monday (August 10, 2026), a bridge in the Niti Valley region was swept away after rising water levels triggered a strong current in the river. A video of the incident showed a large volume of muddy water surging downstream and crashing into the metal bridge. The powerful current soon uprooted the structure and pushed it towards the riverbank.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Health Minister apologises after disability rights activists protest against his use of expression
World.content:
Chennai

Disability rights activists in the city protested the use of an expression (in Tamil) by Health Minister K.G. Arunraj to describe people with disabilities, which they claimed had gone out of use.

The Minister was speaking at the in-person counselling for MBBS and BDS admission for students belonging to special categories (sports quota, ex-servicemen, and people with disabilities) and 7.5% horizontal reservation categories at the Tamil Nadu Government Multi Super-Speciality Hospital, Omandurar Government Estate. After the statement went viral on social media, the Minister tendered an apology on his X account.

“Speaking at the event, while referring to students with disabilities, I deeply regret having inadvertently used an expression that should be avoided as per convention,” Dr. Arunraj wrote on his X handle.

World.title: Delhi govt. revises plan, new Secretariat to come up at ITO
World.content:
PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Sing on Thursday said that the Delhi government has updated its plan for the new Delhi Secretariat, which will now be built on a 10-acre plot after demolishing the current Income Tax office (ITO). The ITO and other government offices will be shifted to a new multi-storey building on an eight-acre plot on the opposite side of the road.

The Delhi government had earlier planned a twin-tower project for the new Delhi Secretariat, which has been changed to single tower in 10 acres of land.

The minister said that the Delhi government had discussions with the IT Department and is going forward with the plan, which has been sent to the Centre. Once the plan is finalised, the government will float a tender for the construction of the building.

Mr. Singh said that as per the plan, the Delhi government will redevelop a total 18 acres of land around ITO, out of which five acres of land belong to the IT office. Once the area is redeveloped, the IT Office will be given space proportional to its total land area.

Currently, several offices of the Delhi government are scattered across the city and there is a space crunch in the present Delhi Secretariat, which is at the Players Building near Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium.

World.title: U.P. teaching job aspirants to run social media campaign for recruitment
World.content:
Teaching job aspirants in Uttar Pradesh will run a social media campaign on August 16 to press the State government to initiate a recruitment drive for primary school teachers.

The aspirants alleged that the government had not conducted a major recruitment drive for primary-level teachers in more than five years, leaving lakhs of eligible candidates waiting for appointments.

“There hasn’t been a major teacher recruitment drive in Uttar Pradesh for over five years at the primary level. Millions of candidates are constantly waiting for teacher recruitment. It has been reported several times that the government will conduct recruitment, but the notification has not been issued,” said Vijay Pratap, an aspirant from Prayagraj.

The campaign, to be run across social media platforms, will seek the immediate issuance of a recruitment notification and a time-bound schedule for completing the appointment process. The organisers said they were targeting 10 million posts on X on August 16.

Several education-related social media platforms run by students and aspirants in the State have circulated the campaign announcement. “All friends should be ready and spread the information about this campaign to as many candidates as possible. Unity is our strength,” read a message that went viral on X.

The Prayagraj-based Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, an organisation of competitive examination aspirants, has also extended its support.

‘Prime years wasted’

Adarsh Tiwari, a D.El.Ed degree holder and another aspirant, said candidates had approached officials, including the Basic Education Minister and Deputy Chief Minister, but had received no assurance on recruitment.

“It has been over five years and no vacancy has come at the primary school level. People with D.El.Ed degrees are feeling helpless because of the neglect. Without appointments, what is the need for such degrees? Five years is a long time in one’s life and our prime young years are being wasted,” he said.

The Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) is a two-year full-time teacher education programme for those seeking to teach Classes 1 to 8.

The Congress supported the proposed campaign and accused the BJP government of failing to provide employment opportunities to the State’s youth.

“The anxiety of aspirants is leading to such online campaigns. We fully stand with the youth of Uttar Pradesh,” said Abhishek Dutt, national secretary of the Congress and zonal in-charge of the Purvanchal zone.

Mr. Dutt said the party would support the aspirants in their efforts to press the government for recruitment.

World.title: Slip road bridges opened over Ghazipur Drain, Hindon Canal in Delhi
World.content:
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday inaugurated two newly constructed two-lane slip road bridges over the Ghazipur Drain and Hindon Canal in east Delhi’s Kondli.

The construction of these bridges will provide thousands of residents of the Trilokpuri, Kondli and Patparganj Assembly constituencies with better road connectivity, smoother movement and a more convenient traffic system. The project will also play an important role in strengthening connectivity in the area and making movement easier for daily commuters, as per the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the Delhi government is focused on developing infrastructure that directly and widely benefits the common people. Strengthening the road network, reducing traffic pressure and ensuring better connectivity between different parts of Delhi are among the government’s priorities. The Kondli project is another important step towards a better-connected, smoother and more developed Delhi. Work is being carried out continuously across different parts of Delhi to improve road infrastructure while also ensuring safe and smooth traffic movement.

Ms. Gupta also said that Delhi had long needed modernisation of its drainage system, but despite growing population and changing needs, adequate attention was not given to the improvement, desilting and maintenance of old drains and the drainage network. “This resulted in waterlogging and inconvenience to citizens during the rains. The present government is working to strengthen the drainage system and find a permanent solution to the problem of waterlogging,” she said.

World.title: Instagram changes its wordmark logo after over a decade
World.content:
Meta introduced a refreshed Instagram wordmark logo on Thursday (August 13, 2026)

The change was announced by Instagram head Adam Mosseri on both Instagram and Threads, where he described the new logo as “sharper and more modern” while still referencing the original and maintaining simplicity, as per TechCrunch.

The new wordmark keeps the familiar script style, with redrawn letterforms.

The last time Instagram updated its design was 2016, when the company moved away from the classic brown camera with the rainbow stripe to the colorful pink gradient that remains the icon today.

“The wordmark at the top of the app hasn’t changed in 10 years, so it was time for a refresh,” Instagram head Adam Mosseri wrote in a post on the platform. “Cleaner and more modern, with references to the original and the simplicity and craft that’s always made it Instagram.”

Some liked it, while many found it disappointing.

Many joked that the logo now looks like it reads “Instagzam” because of the shape of the font used for the “r.”

World.title: Protect farmers’ rights before cement project, Meghalaya tribal body tells govt.
World.content:
An apex body representing an indigenous community in Meghalaya has given the State government 10 days to ensure that the rights of landowners and farmers are protected before proceeding with an integrated cement plant and limestone mining project in the Lum Syrman area of East Jaintia Hills district.

The ₹1,800-crore project has faced opposition since May, when protests by a section of local stakeholders forced district authorities to call off public hearings.

On Thursday, a delegation of the Jaintia National Council (JNC), led by its general secretary Wanshwa Suting, submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma seeking immediate government intervention over Shree Cement Limited’s proposed limestone project covering 217.394 hectares in Lum Syrman.

“The rights of the landowners and farmers of Sutnga and Nongkhlieh Elakas (traditional administrative units) must be protected and preserved before any further irreversible step is allowed in favour of the proposed mining project,” the JNC said.

The organisation said the customary, possession, cultivation and user rights of landowners and farmers in the two Elakas were linked to the Lum Syrman area.

It said the issue of land “cannot simply be treated as an environmental or industrial clearance matter” without addressing the concerns of local residents who would be affected by the project. It demanded a time-bound and transparent verification of revenue, registration, customary, cultivation and other official records before the project proceeds.

The JNC also said farmers’ livelihoods “cannot be brushed aside in the name of mineral development” and called for “fair and lawful compensation for the loss (resulting from the project)”, subject to the determination of the respective legal and customary rights.

“It seems that the State government is favouring these cement companies, even to the extent of blocking residents from attending the public hearing held on July 31. If the government is confident that everything has been done fairly and transparently, why should ordinary residents and affected landholders face obstacles in exercising their right to participate?” Mr. Suting said.

The JNC said its opposition was not to development but to the project being pursued without ensuring justice, transparency and protection of the rights of local stakeholders.

World.title: Minerals belong to Jharkhand, land belongs to Jharkhand: CM
World.content:
Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Thursday strongly opposed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to restrict States’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands.

The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on Wednesday while the Rajya Sabha cleared it on Thursday, completing the parliamentary approval process. The Bill will become a law after receiving the President’s assent.

Calling the legislation a “black Bill” and an injustice to the people of Jharkhand, Mr. Soren warned of a massive agitation against the Centre’s move. “The entire nation will witness. Minerals belong to Jharkhand, land belongs to Jharkhand; so why should Delhi decide on our rights and entitlements? In haste, the Central government passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, effectively tying Jharkhand’s hands and feet,” he wrote on X.

Jharkhand holds about 40% of the country’s total minerals.

“It is a severe blow to their development and future. Jharkhand will not tolerate this stepmotherly treatment. In Jharkhand, schemes providing social security to millions – such as the Maiya Samman Yojana, Abua Awas Yojana, pensions, education, health, and others – will be on the verge of closure. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha strongly opposes this,” the Chief Minister said.

Mr. Soren added that there will be fierce opposition to the move in “every district, every block, every panchayat, every town”.

“If the Central government does not come to its senses and fails to restore to Jharkhand and its people their rights and entitlements, Jharkhand will not shy away from taking decisive and historic decisions either,” he said.

World.title: Yadgar-i-Fatah monument inaugurated in Islamabad on eve of Independence Day
World.content:
The Yadgar-i-Fatah monument, built to honour Pakistan’s martyrs and commemorate Marka-i-Haq, was inaugurated by President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Thursday night, on the eve of the country’s 80th Independence Day.

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu and Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf were in attendance and stood for the national anthem, played by a military band.

Foreign diplomats, military attaches, officers of the three services and other senior officials were also in attendance.

(From L-R) Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attend the inauguration ceremony of the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/ISPR Official

‘Guarantor of peace’

Addressing the ceremony, Prime Minister Shehbaz congratulated the nation on Independence Day and said that under Quaid-i-Azam’s leadership, “we entered the realm of freedom from the darkness of slavery. Our elders sacrificed their lives and property”.

“Yadgar-i-Fatah symbolises our resolve and determination and the domination of our armed forces over the enemy,” he added.

The premier also congratulated the nation on Marka-i-Haq and paid tribute to Field Marshal Munir for his leadership during the conflict, as well as Air Chief Marshal Sidhu and Admiral Ashraf.

“Under his leadership, we defeated the enemy,” PM Shehbaz said.

Paying tribute to the architects and engineers who designed the monument, the premier expressed appreciation for its sleek design and eight-month completion time.

“Its completion in eight months would not have been possible if the field marshal hadn’t invested his deep interest,” PM Shehbaz added.

“This is not just a monument of blocks, but a tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives to defend the nation. That triumph is the victory of our army and our people, and this is our pride.”

He noted that Pakistan wants peace, not war, and that desiring peace should not be perceived as a sign of weakness.

“With dignity and determination, we are resolute for peace,” the premier stated, adding that Pakistan had been recognised as a “guarantor of peace” in the region.

“If anyone challenges Pakistan’s sovereignty and defence, they will receive an even stronger reply than in May 2025,” he warned.

PM Shehbaz noted that after suffering defeat, India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty unilaterally.

“I warn that every drop of water is our red line. If India does not keep on the right track, we will give it a direct response,” he further warned.

Speaking about the future of the country, PM Shehbaz recognised that doors needed to be opened for the younger generation.

“We need to incorporate the latest technology to advance in the journey of our economic progress. We need to develop our human resources so our country will enter into a new phase of progress and well-being,” he stressed.

“We must make a Pakistan where all provinces, including Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, will advance and develop together.”

A world free of conflict

The premier added that the nation wants to see a world “free from all sorts of conflict”.

“We want to resolve all the issues with justice and in accordance with the UN Charter,” he emphasised, highlighting Islamabad’s role as a mediator between Iran and the US in the ongoing Middle East War.

“The Makkah Agreement is the promise of peace for the Middle East, and a hope of peace for the Muslim world. It is also a message of peace for the whole world,” PM Shehbaz added.

He further stated that Pakistan would keep advocating for the oppressed Palestinians and supporting their right to self-determination, while adding that Islamabad wants peace in Afghanistan, but the use of its soil for cross-border terrorism was “unacceptable”.

“We need to stay united for peace and development. We need to bury the hate and revive the love for each other by forgetting our differences,” he emphasised.

‘We are not a small country to play with’

Taking the podium, President Zardari said that the nation and its armed forces, under Field Marshal Munir’s dynamic leadership, gave a befitting answer to India during the war last year.

“This is in faith to remember what happened, in how many days it happened, where it happened, and this will go down in history for everyone to remember, whether today or the day after,” he said.

He noted that Pakistan’s military response to Indian aggression demonstrated that “we are not a small country for you to play with”.

“We are there as partners to the world, in the … family of countries,” President Zardari added. “And I think, today, even they understand that Pakistan is a national partner.”

He added that the monument reflects the unity of the nation, the strength of the armed forces and the sacrifices given. The president recalled that his own father was called upon by Quaid-i-Azam to fight in the 1948 Kashmir War.

“Most of Sindh, KP, other places, anybody who could carry an arm were there, and they fought against the Indian Army,” he stated. “By the grace of God, we got our Durand Line, our border line, but still so, a lot needs to be done … by us, the people and the public and definitely, the coming generation of Pakistan.”

President Zardari noted that the premier, the CDF, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi were playing a “most commendable and praiseworthy” role.

“We’ve been successful till now. Life comes and goes … we’ve seen tragedies, we’ve seen successes [and] successfully managed to guide our system through,” he added. “I’m not saying there would not be weaknesses; there always are; but there is no nation in the world that can claim they have no weaknesses.”

Prior to the speeches by the country’s leadership, visuals broadcast on television showed a large contingent of personnel from the military, paramilitary forces and police presenting a guard of honour, accompanied by a military band.

Personnel from the military, paramilitary forces and police present their standards during the inauguration ceremony of the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/ISPR Official

Yadgar-i-Fatah monument

The marble monument was completed within eight months and features five archways, which represent the five pillars of Islam, as well as the five pillars of Pakistan itself — the government, the military, the media, the people and the ideology underpinning the nation.

Additionally, they represent the three branches of the military — the Army, the Air Force and the Navy — as well as cyber-defence and space warfare.

As part of the inauguration, a light and sound show was presented with moving images projected directly onto the monument, state television showed. One of the sequences highlighted the history of Pakistan and its military up until Marka-i-Haq.

Iconic moments from the May war were also projected onto the monument, such as when villagers and Punjab Rangers shot at Indian drones together.

Moving graphics are directly projected onto the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument during its inauguration ceremony in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/PTV News

Following the light show, Pakistan Air Force fighter jets performed a flypast over the monument, deploying flares in the night sky.

A Pakistan Air Force fighter jet performs a flypast over the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/PTV News

The monument marks Pakistan’s victory over India in a brief military conflict last May.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs0.45, high-speed diesel by Rs1.16
World.content:
The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.16.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325.43 per litre while HSD will cost Rs383.95 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 14 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.
